successIndicators: Organise correct roles without extended instruction.
Win or neutralise the first phase.
Adapt to changing restart types and locations.
matchApplication: Matches contain frequent changes between centre bounces, boundary throw-ins, free kicks, marks and kick-ins. Teams must organise rapidly because delays create uncontested possession and structural mismatches.

title: Match-Simulation Foundation Phase Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating foundational match-simulation behaviours across continuous and varied phases.
objective: Assess whether the team can independently apply the foundational match-simulation behaviours developed in MS-001 to MS-019 across connected phases of live Australian football.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with full positional roles.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Prepare six starting scenarios covering defensive intercept, kick-mark possession, corridor access, wing contest, forward entry and stoppage.
Assign coaches to observe specific team behaviours.
Play three blocks of eight to ten minutes.
Use minimal coach intervention during each block.
Begin each block from a different scenario.
Require player leaders to organise feedback between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the first starting scenario.
Teams organise and begin live play.
After the initial phase, play continues without restriction.
Coaches assess structure, decision making, communication, skill execution and transition.
Natural stoppages and turnovers are played under normal match conditions.
At the end of the block, teams receive a two-minute player-led review.
The second block begins from a different phase and scoreboard condition.
The final block begins without the scenario being announced until players reach the starting position.
Award points for the match score and nominated tactical behaviours.
Finish with individual and team ratings against the success indicators.
coachingPoints: Players must recognise the current phase without waiting for coach instruction.
The team should maintain balance between possession, territory and attacking risk.
Defensive structures must remain connected behind the football.
The first possession after a contest or turnover must have purpose.
Forward entries should match the available options.
Restarts require immediate organisation.
Communication should continue throughout all phases.
Players must apply feedback from earlier blocks.
Coaches should assess repeatability, not isolated successful moments.

commonErrors.error: Players perform well only in the announced starting phase.
commonErrors.correction: Continue assessing structure after play becomes unpredictable.

commonErrors.error: Teams rely on coaches to organise restarts.
commonErrors.correction: Require player leaders to call roles and match-ups.

commonErrors.error: Attacking numbers move ahead of the football without protection.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected support behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Forward entries are rushed after long possession chains.
commonErrors.correction: Reassess the forward structure before the final disposal.

commonErrors.error: Feedback does not transfer into later blocks.
commonErrors.correction: Assign a player leader responsibility for reinforcing the correction.

progressions: Play a full quarter without coach interruption.
Add interchange restrictions and fatigue.
Use hidden scoreboard objectives for each team.
Record the simulation for detailed tactical review.
Require players to complete self-assessment before coach feedback.
regressions: Use four starting scenarios rather than six.
Reduce ground size and player numbers.
Provide player leaders with tactical reminder cards.
successIndicators: Recognise and organise for changing match phases.
Use the corridor without forcing risk.
Connect stoppage wins to attacking outcomes.
matchApplication: This assessment completes the foundational stage of the Match Simulation chapter. It tests whether players can combine restart organisation, possession control, contest work, transition, forward connection and defensive response within continuous football rather than treating each skill as an isolated exercise.
relatedDrills: MS-013 – Corridor Access and Release Simulation

title: Defensive Switch Movement Simulation
primarySkill: Moving collectively to create and complete a defensive-half switch.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move the opposition across the ground, create a viable far-side option and complete a defensive-half switch without losing structural protection.
groundSize: Defensive goal line to approximately 20 metres beyond the centre of the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one team in possession across defensive 50 and half-back.
Organise the opposition in a forward-half press.
Mark wide exit gates on both sides of the ground and a central gate beyond defensive 50.
Begin each repetition with possession on one boundary side.
Require the far-side defenders, wing and high forward to begin in realistic match positions.
The possession team attempts to move the opposition and exit through the opposite side.
The pressing team attempts to intercept and score.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins with a mark near one defensive pocket.
Nearby players create short options while far-side players move into switch positions.
The ball carrier may play short, backward or lateral to change the angle.
The opposition shifts its press with the football.
The possession team attempts to complete the switch and exit through the opposite wide gate or central gate.
Award three points for a switch followed by a controlled central exit.
Award two points for a switch followed by a wide exit.
Award the pressing team three points for a turnover and goal.
Continue until a successful exit, score, stoppage or turnover.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: The far side must move before the football is kicked across the ground.
Players should create different depths rather than forming a flat line.
The first backward possession should open the ground rather than simply surrender territory.
The switch receiver must scan before possession arrives.
The wing and high forward should provide the next connection after the switch.
Players behind the football must remain connected in case of turnover.
The team should accelerate once the opposition press is displaced.
Communication must identify whether the switch is open, delayed or closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether far-side players move early enough.
The depth and angle of switch options.
Whether backward possession improves the next kick.
The switch receiver’s body position and scanning.
Connection from the switch to the wing or corridor.

commonErrors.error: Far-side players remain stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement as soon as possession is secured on the opposite side.

commonErrors.error: Players line up at the same depth.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger short, medium and long options.

commonErrors.error: The switch is kicked too slowly.
commonErrors.correction: Move the football quickly once the far side opens.

commonErrors.error: The receiver faces the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Arrive side-on and scan the inside before receiving.

commonErrors.error: All players run forward after the switch.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain at least one connected option behind possession.

progressions: Allow the opposition to change between zone and man-on-man pressure.
Reduce the time allowed to complete the switch.
Continue play to the opposite goal.
Begin with the possession team temporarily outnumbered.
Add a late-game possession-retention scenario.
regressions: Remove one or two opposition pressure players.
Freeze the opposition during the first two disposals.
Allow the coach to guide player positioning.
successIndicators: Create the far-side option before the football arrives.
Move the opposition across the ground.
Complete the switch without unnecessary risk.
matchApplication: Defensive switches are effective only when the entire team moves with the football. This simulation trains the coordinated off-ball movement required to transfer possession from one side of the ground to the other and escape an organised press.
relatedDrills: MS-013 – Corridor Access and Release Simulation

title: Forward-Line Rotation After Turnover Simulation
primarySkill: Rotating forward roles immediately after the team wins possession.
objective: Develop the forward line’s ability to rotate high, deep and lateral roles after a turnover so that the ball carrier receives multiple separated attacking options.
groundSize: From half-back to the attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one team across half-back and midfield with forwards inside 50.
Position the opposition in attacking shape before the turnover.
Start each repetition with an intercept, ground-ball win or pressured turnover at half-back.
Assign initial high, deep and lateral forward roles.
Once possession changes, forwards may rotate roles according to the location of the football.
The defending team transitions to protect the corridor and goal.
Rotate forward combinations regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with an opposition forward entry or loose-ball situation.
The defending team wins possession and begins transition.
Forwards immediately recognise the turnover and rotate into high, deep and lateral options.
The highest forward may provide connection, while deeper forwards preserve scoring space.
The ball carrier selects the best available forward option.
Play continues until a score, defensive rebound or stoppage.
Award three points for a goal created from a clear rotation.
Award two points for a mark inside 30 metres.
Award the defending team two points for an intercept and controlled exit.
Reset with different starting forward positions.
coachingPoints: Forwards must react to the turnover before the ball carrier reaches midfield.
One forward should provide a high connection without emptying the scoring zone.
Deep forwards should maintain separation and avoid all leading toward the football.
Lateral movement can create a central lane for another player.
The ball carrier should recognise which rotation has created the best option.
Ground-level support must move beneath likely contests.
Forwards must transition to pressure if the entry is intercepted.
Communication should identify role changes early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Reaction speed of the forward line.
Whether high and deep roles remain balanced.
The relationship between forward movement and ball-carrier position.
Forward pressure after a defensive win.

commonErrors.error: All forwards lead toward the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one high option while others preserve depth and width.

commonErrors.error: Rotation begins too late.
commonErrors.correction: Move as soon as the turnover is won.

commonErrors.error: Deep space becomes empty.
commonErrors.correction: Keep at least one dangerous player close to goal.

commonErrors.error: Forwards cross into the same lane.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate role changes and use separate channels.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after the entry is intercepted.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate forward pressure and protect the exit.

progressions: Allow defenders to change between man-on-man and zone.
Add greater pressure on the half-back ball carrier.
Require forwards to rotate without preset roles.
Continue full-ground play after a defensive rebound.
Introduce scoreboard and time conditions.
regressions: Nominate the high and deep rotation before each repetition.
Pause after the turnover to organise forward movement.
successIndicators: Establish high, deep and lateral roles.
Preserve dangerous space close to goal.
Apply pressure after a failed entry.
matchApplication: Forward structures must change rapidly when possession is won unexpectedly. This simulation develops the movement required to convert defensive turnovers into organised scoring opportunities before the opposition resets.

title: Midfield Wave Running Simulation
primarySkill: Creating continuous midfield support through staggered wave running.
objective: Develop the midfield group’s ability to provide repeated support ahead of, beside and behind the football without compressing into the same running lane.
groundSize: A central area approximately 90–120 metres long and 55–70 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark three longitudinal running lanes across the playing area.
Position an attacking group at one end and defenders throughout the middle.
Begin with a turnover or possession win at half-back.
Attackers move the football through staggered support waves.
Defenders attempt to delay the attack and force lateral movement.
Place recovering defenders behind the initial play.
Rotate inside and outside midfield roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football to the attacking team.
The first wave provides immediate forward and lateral support.
The second wave follows behind the football to receive a release or protect turnover.
Players may carry, handball or kick according to pressure.
Defenders attempt to close the central lanes.
Recovering defenders enter after three seconds.
Award three points for reaching the scoring zone with three connected support efforts.
Award two points for a controlled entry created by a second-wave runner.
Award the defending team two points for delaying the attack for 15 seconds.
Reset from the opposite direction.
coachingPoints: Support runners should stagger their depth rather than run in a straight line.
The first wave threatens forward space.
The second wave remains available behind or lateral to possession.
Players should run into open lanes rather than directly toward the football.
The ball carrier should release only after drawing pressure.
Communication must identify overlap and inside options.
Players who dispose must continue supporting the play.
After turnover, all runners must recover through the corridor.

commonErrors.error: Support runners move at the same depth.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger first, second and trailing waves.

commonErrors.error: Players run directly toward the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Attack free space and create a passing angle.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier releases too early.
commonErrors.correction: Draw an opponent before disposing.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after giving the football.
commonErrors.correction: Continue to the next support position.

commonErrors.error: No runner remains behind possession.
commonErrors.correction: Keep a trailing wave connected to the football.

progressions: Increase defender numbers.
Reduce the width of the running lanes.
Require a scoring shot at the end of the transition.
Allow full contact and live counterattack.
Add a repeat transition immediately after the first score.
regressions: Reduce the distance to the scoring zone.
matchApplication: Effective transition requires more than one supporting runner. This simulation develops the repeated midfield movement that allows a team to continue advancing after the first disposal while remaining protected against turnover.
relatedDrills: MS-022 – Forward-Line Rotation After Turnover Simulation

title: High-Forward Rotation Simulation
primarySkill: Rotating high forwards to connect midfield possession with the scoring zone.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to use coordinated high-forward movement to create connection options while preserving space for deeper forwards.
groundSize: From the centre of the ground to the attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position midfielders around the centre and forwards inside attacking 50.
Assign two high-forward starting positions and two deeper targets.
Position defenders in realistic match-ups.
Begin each repetition with midfield possession under pressure.
High forwards may rotate toward the football, across the ground or into deeper space.
Deep forwards adjust to preserve separation.
Rotate roles every four repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession near the centre.
One high forward presents as a connection option.
The second high forward moves laterally, deeper or beyond the first receiver.
Deep forwards preserve scoring space and coordinate their leads.
The football is moved through the high-forward line or directly inside 50.
Play continues until a score, defensive rebound or stoppage.
Award two points for a clean high-forward connection.
Award three points if that connection produces a mark inside 30 metres.
Award the defending team two points for an intercept and exit.
Reset with altered starting positions.
coachingPoints: Only one high forward should enter the same connection space at a time.
The second high forward should create the next option.
Deep forwards must not follow every movement toward the football.
Receivers should arrive side-on and scan before possession.
High-forward movement should improve the next disposal.
Midfielders should recognise when bypassing the high forward is appropriate.
Forward pressure begins immediately after turnover.
Communication must clarify who is presenting and who is preserving depth.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Connection to the next forward movement.

commonErrors.error: Both high forwards lead to the same location.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one presenter and one secondary mover.

commonErrors.error: Deep forwards follow the ball too far.
commonErrors.correction: Hold dangerous space close to goal.

commonErrors.error: The receiver marks facing backward.
commonErrors.correction: Lead on an angle and arrive side-on.

commonErrors.error: High-forward possession does not improve the attack.
commonErrors.correction: Move or dispose quickly to create the next forward entry.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and close the nearest exit.

progressions: Increase midfield pressure.
Allow defenders to zone off their direct opponents.
Remove preset high-forward roles.
Add a time limit for generating a shot.
Continue play to the opposite goal after a turnover.
regressions: Increase the space between defensive lines.
Pause after the first connection to coach movement.
successIndicators: Receive in a position to continue play.
matchApplication: High forwards are essential in connecting midfield possession to the scoring zone. This simulation develops the coordinated movement required to provide an option without drawing the entire forward line away from goal.
relatedDrills: MS-022 – Forward-Line Rotation After Turnover Simulation

title: Defensive Overlap Exit Simulation
primarySkill: Creating an overlap to escape defensive pressure.
objective: Develop the defensive group’s ability to generate an overlap through immediate running support after winning possession inside defensive 50.
groundSize: Defensive goal line to approximately 20 metres beyond defensive 50.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position defenders inside defensive 50 and opposition forwards in a pressing structure.
Mark central and wide exit gates beyond defensive 50.
Begin with an intercept, spoil or ground-ball win.
One defender starts behind the initial possession to create the first overlap option.
Additional defenders may join through running support.
The opposition applies immediate pressure.
Rotate initial ball winners and overlap runners.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into defensive 50.
A defender wins or receives possession.
The nearest support player runs past or to the outside to create an overlap.
The ball carrier decides whether to release, carry or kick.
Additional defenders support the next possession.
The team attempts to exit through a marked gate.
Award three points for a central exit created by an overlap.
Award two points for a wide exit.
Award the attacking team three points for a turnover and goal.
Reset with a new entry and overlap starting point.
coachingPoints: The overlap runner should accelerate immediately after possession is secured.
The runner must choose a lane that improves the ball carrier’s angle.
The ball carrier should draw pressure before releasing.
Support should continue after the first handball.
The team must avoid handballing into tighter pressure.
A kicking option should remain available outside the overlap chain.
Defenders behind the football must protect against turnover.
Communication should identify pressure and release timing.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed and angle of the overlap run.
Whether the ball carrier commits an opponent.
Use of central and wide exits.

commonErrors.error: The overlap runner moves too close to the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Run wider to create separation and a better angle.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier releases before drawing pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Carry at the defender before handballing.

commonErrors.error: The support chain ends after one disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue running to support the next possession.

commonErrors.error: Players handball into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Use the overlap only when it improves space.

commonErrors.error: No player remains behind possession.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one defender connected to protect turnover.

progressions: Add another opposition pressure forward.
Require two connected overlap efforts before exiting.
Continue full-ground transition after the exit.
Begin with a loose ground ball rather than controlled possession.
Add a time limit for escaping defensive 50.
regressions: Increase the width of the exit gates.
matchApplication: Defensive teams often escape pressure through running support rather than stationary kicking options. This simulation develops the coordinated overlap movement required to turn a defensive possession into attacking transition.

title: Switch-to-Corridor Acceleration Simulation
primarySkill: Accelerating through the corridor after completing a lateral switch.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to use a switch to move the opposition and then accelerate decisively through newly opened central space.
groundSize: Defensive 50 to the attacking goal across two-thirds of a ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark a central corridor and two wide lanes.
Position one team in possession on a defensive wing.
Organise the opposition in a shifted press.
Establish far-side switch options and central receivers.
Position forwards inside attacking 50.
The possession team must first move the football laterally before deciding whether central access is available.
Rotate starting sides.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins near one boundary.
Players complete two or more lateral possessions to move the opposition.
Central receivers adjust their position as the press shifts.
Once the corridor opens, the team may accelerate through it.
Supporting players run ahead, lateral and behind the central receiver.
Play continues to a forward entry and score.
Award three points for a corridor entry followed by a shot.
Award two points for a controlled inside-50 entry after the switch.
Award the opposition three points for a central intercept.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: The switch should move the opposition before the team attacks centrally.
Central receivers must move with the press rather than remain fixed.
The corridor entry should occur at speed.
The receiver should know the next option before possession arrives.
Support runners must maintain separate lanes.
Wide options should remain available if the corridor closes.
Players behind the football must guard against central turnover.
Tempo should change clearly from controlled switch to aggressive attack.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the switch genuinely shifts the opposition.

commonErrors.error: The corridor is entered before the opposition moves.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the switch and wait for central space to open.

commonErrors.error: Central receivers remain stationary.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust position with each lateral possession.

commonErrors.error: The tempo remains slow after entry.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate immediately once central access is gained.

commonErrors.error: Support runners enter the same lane.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger depth and maintain separate channels.

commonErrors.error: The team forces central play when it closes.
commonErrors.correction: Release wide and retain possession.

progressions: Allow the opposition to disguise its central coverage.
Reduce the time available after the switch.
Require a goal rather than any shot.
Continue play live after a central turnover.
Begin with greater opposition numbers around the corridor.
regressions: Reduce pressure on the final forward entry.
successIndicators: Shift the opposition with lateral possession.
Move central receivers into available space.
Recognise the correct moment to accelerate.
matchApplication: The most damaging switches do more than change sides. They displace the opposition and create central access. This simulation develops the movement and tempo change required to convert a lateral switch into direct attack.
relatedDrills: MS-013 – Corridor Access and Release Simulation

title: Full-Ground Lateral Shift Simulation
primarySkill: Shifting the entire team laterally with the movement of the football.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move as a connected unit across the ground while preserving attacking width and defensive coverage.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Mark three vertical lanes across the ground.
Begin with one team in possession at half-back.
Both teams must shift laterally as the football moves between lanes.
Coaches observe the spacing between defensive, midfield and forward lines.
Play continues to goal.
Rotate starting possession and field position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins in one wide lane.
Players move the football laterally or forward according to available options.
All three lines adjust their position with each change of lane.
The defending team shifts to protect the corridor and the next likely possession.
The attacking team maintains far-side width while keeping support near the football.
Play continues until a score, turnover or defensive exit.
Award two points for maintaining connected team spacing through a full switch.
Award three points for scoring after a successful lateral shift.
Award the defending team two points for forcing play to the boundary and winning possession.
Reset from a different starting lane.
coachingPoints: The team must move with the football rather than watch it move.
Nearby players provide support while far-side players preserve width.
Defensive lines should shift without becoming excessively narrow.
The distance between lines must remain manageable.
Players behind the football should remain connected to the attack.
Forwards should adjust laterally to create new leading lanes.
Communication should identify the open side and dangerous opposition players.
After turnover, the team must reverse its shift immediately.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whole-team movement with each change of lane.

commonErrors.error: Players remain in their original positions.
commonErrors.correction: Shift with every change in ball location.

commonErrors.error: The defensive team collapses too narrowly.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor while retaining outside coverage.

commonErrors.error: The attacking far side moves too close.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the switch is available.

commonErrors.error: Large gaps open between lines.
commonErrors.correction: Keep defensive, midfield and forward units connected.

commonErrors.error: Players continue shifting the wrong way after turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Reverse roles and movement immediately.

progressions: Increase the speed of ball movement.
Remove lane markers.
Allow full match-like contact.
Add time and scoreboard pressure.
Play an uninterrupted full quarter.
regressions: Pause after each switch to correct team positioning.
Limit play to half a ground.
matchApplication: Team structure depends on collective movement. This simulation teaches players that every lateral disposal requires positional adjustment across the entire ground, not only from those closest to the football.

title: Fast-Restart Spread Simulation
primarySkill: Creating immediate movement and spread after a fast restart.
objective: Develop both teams’ ability to organise rapidly when play restarts from a mark, free kick, out-on-the-full decision or quick stoppage release.
groundSize: Half to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the squad into two teams.
Prepare starting points for marks, free kicks, out-on-the-full restarts and quick stoppage releases.
Place players in realistic match positions around each restart.
The coach signals the restart with limited warning.
The team in possession attempts to use immediate movement and spread.
The defending team protects dangerous space and identifies match-ups.
Rotate restart locations and possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach signals a restart type and location.
The team in possession immediately spreads into short, long, lateral and behind options.
The ball carrier decides whether to play on quickly or hold possession.
The defending team guards the corridor and likely next options.
Play continues for 30–45 seconds.
Award two points for creating three clear options within five seconds.
Award three points for converting the restart into a scoring opportunity.
Award the defending team two points for denying the first movement and forcing a turnover.
Reset immediately at a different location.
Complete eight to twelve restarts.
coachingPoints: Movement must begin as soon as the restart is recognised.
Players should create different depths and angles.
The ball carrier should not play on merely because the restart is fast.
The nearest defender guards immediate play-on space.
Other defenders identify the next most dangerous receivers.
Players behind the football must remain connected.
Communication should identify play-on, hold and switch options.
Both teams must anticipate the next phase.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Decision to play on or hold.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for the ball carrier to direct them.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement immediately when the restart is recognised.

commonErrors.error: All options lead short.
commonErrors.correction: Create short, long, lateral and behind support.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier plays on into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Hold possession when movement has not created an advantage.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase the football only.
commonErrors.correction: Guard dangerous space and identify the next receiver.

commonErrors.error: The team ignores the next phase.
commonErrors.correction: Organise support beyond the first disposal.

progressions: Reduce the warning before each restart.
Add scoreboard and time conditions.
Use quick consecutive restarts.
Remove coach communication.
Continue each repetition until a score.
regressions: Use only marks and free kicks initially.
successIndicators: Maintain support beyond the first disposal.
matchApplication: Fast restarts can create attacking opportunities before the opposition organises. They can also cause costly turnovers when players move without structure. This simulation develops controlled urgency around match restarts.

title: Rotational Match-Up Handover Simulation
primarySkill: Handing over opponents while maintaining defensive team structure.
objective: Develop the defensive team’s ability to pass opponents between players as the football moves without creating unguarded space or duplicated coverage.
groundSize: From the centre to one attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position an attacking team across midfield and forward 50.
Organise the defending team in a zone or hybrid structure.
Mark three vertical lanes to assist observation.
Begin with attacking possession on one wing.
Attackers rotate, cross and change depth as the football moves.
Defenders must communicate whether to follow, hand over or hold space.
If defenders win possession, they counterattack through an exit gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team moves the football laterally and forward.
Attackers rotate between high, deep, central and wide positions.
Defenders communicate each movement.
A defender may follow an opponent, pass the opponent to a teammate or protect a dangerous zone.
Play continues until a score, intercept or defensive exit.
Award the attacking team three points for a score created by an unguarded rotation.
Award the defending team two points for completing three successful handovers.
Award three defensive points for an intercept followed by an exit.
Reset from the opposite side.
Rotate defensive units and attacking roles.
coachingPoints: Defenders must communicate before releasing an opponent.
The receiving defender should confirm the handover.
Dangerous central space takes priority over low-threat outside movement.
Players should avoid two defenders following the same opponent.
The deepest defender should organise the line.
Defenders must shift with the football while maintaining vision of opponents.
After an intercept, the team should spread immediately.
Communication should be short, early and specific.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing and clarity of handover calls.
Protection of central and goal-side space.

commonErrors.error: A defender releases an opponent without communication.
commonErrors.correction: Call the handover and receive confirmation first.

commonErrors.error: Two defenders follow the same player.
commonErrors.correction: One takes the opponent while the other protects structure.

commonErrors.error: Defenders protect low-threat wide space and expose the corridor.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise central and goal-side danger.

commonErrors.error: Players watch the football and lose opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain vision of both the football and nearby threats.

commonErrors.error: Defenders remain compressed after intercepting.
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately into exit positions.

progressions: Remove lane markers.
Allow attackers to rotate without restrictions.
Add more high-speed ball movement.
Continue full-ground transition after an intercept.
Include scoreboard scenarios requiring aggressive or conservative defence.
regressions: Limit attackers to one rotation at a time.
successIndicators: Maintain connection across the defensive line.
matchApplication: Modern defensive systems require players to exchange opponents as attackers rotate through different areas. This simulation develops the communication and collective movement required to maintain structure without relying solely on direct match-ups.
relatedDrills: MS-005 – Forward-Half Lock-In and Defensive Exit Simulation

title: Match-Simulation Movement Phase Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating coordinated off-ball movement across attacking, defensive and transition phases.
objective: Assess the team’s ability to apply the coordinated movement principles developed in MS-021 to MS-029 during continuous and changing match situations.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Prepare five starting scenarios covering defensive switch, turnover attack, fast restart, defensive handover and full-ground transition.
Assign coaches specific movement behaviours to assess.
Use three playing blocks of eight to ten minutes.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Require player leaders to organise tactical adjustments between blocks.
Use minimal coach intervention during play.
Begin each block from a different field position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the first starting scenario.
Teams organise and begin live play.
After the initial phase, play continues without movement restrictions.
Coaches assess off-ball movement, spacing, support, line connection and communication.
Natural turnovers and stoppages continue under match conditions.
At the end of each block, teams receive a two-minute player-led review.
The next block begins from a different scenario.
Award points for the match score and nominated movement behaviours.
The final block is played without advance explanation of the starting challenge.
Conclude with team and individual assessment against the success indicators.
coachingPoints: Players must move before the football arrives.
Support should exist ahead, lateral and behind possession.
Forward movement must preserve depth and separation.
Defensive movement must protect dangerous space.
The entire team should shift when the football changes sides.
Tempo should increase when movement creates an advantage.
Communication must support rotations and handovers.
Players must reverse roles immediately after turnover.
Coaches should assess repeatable movement patterns rather than isolated running efforts.

commonErrors.error: Players move only when they expect to receive.
commonErrors.correction: Move to create space and options for teammates.

commonErrors.error: Multiple players occupy the same lane or depth.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger positions and preserve separate channels.

commonErrors.error: Team lines become disconnected.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain manageable spacing between defenders, midfielders and forwards.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to reverse movement after turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Change roles and direction immediately when possession changes.

commonErrors.error: Communication occurs after the movement.
commonErrors.correction: Call rotations, switches and handovers early.

progressions: Play a full quarter without coach interruption.
Remove all field markers.
Add interchange and fatigue restrictions.
Introduce hidden scoreboard objectives.
Record the assessment for detailed review.
regressions: Use three starting scenarios rather than five.
Provide player leaders with movement reminder cards.
successIndicators: Create forward, lateral and behind support.
Maintain width, depth and line connection.
matchApplication: This assessment completes the first movement-focused block of the Match Simulation chapter. It determines whether players can coordinate their movement across defensive exits, switches, forward rotations, transition waves, restarts and defensive handovers within continuous football.

title: Defensive Midfield Fold-Back Simulation
primarySkill: Folding midfielders behind the football when the opposition breaks forward.
objective: Develop the midfield group’s ability to recognise an opposition break, sprint into effective defensive positions and support the back line without collapsing unnecessarily around the football.
groundSize: From the centre square to the defensive goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position an attacking team around the centre and half-forward areas.
Position the defending team with defenders inside defensive 50 and midfielders initially forward of the football.
Mark a central corridor and two wide defensive lanes.
Begin each repetition with the attacking team winning possession near the centre.
Delay the defending midfielders by two to three seconds before allowing them to recover.
The attacking team attempts to create a score.
The defending team attempts to delay the attack, regain numbers and rebound through an exit gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football to the attacking team near the centre.
The attackers move quickly toward goal with an initial numerical advantage.
Defending midfielders react to the turnover and sprint toward defensive positions.
The first recovering midfielder protects the corridor or most dangerous central option.
Additional midfielders identify free opponents, support the back line and defend likely ground-ball locations.
If the defending team wins possession, it attempts to exit through a wide or central gate.
Award the attacking team three points for a goal and two points for a mark inside 30 metres.
Award the defending team two points for preventing a score and three points for completing a controlled exit.
Stop after a score, exit, stoppage or 25 seconds.
Reset with different starting midfield positions.
coachingPoints: Midfielders must react to the possession change immediately.
The first recovery run should protect the most dangerous central space.
Players should run to influence the next possession rather than follow an opponent from behind.
Communication must identify free attackers and available defensive match-ups.
Recovering players should arrive goal side whenever possible.
The midfield must support the defenders without all collapsing inside 30 metres.
One player should remain available for the first rebound possession.
After winning the football, the team should spread quickly into exit positions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Protection of central and goal-side space.
Whether players recover to useful positions.
Rebound support after possession is regained.

commonErrors.error: Midfielders jog back behind the play.
commonErrors.correction: Sprint to the next dangerous space rather than following the football.

commonErrors.error: All recovering players collapse toward the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Protect corridor, free opponents and likely next possessions.

commonErrors.error: Players recover on the wrong side of opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Work to regain goal-side position.

commonErrors.error: Defenders and midfielders cover the same attacker.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate and allocate responsibility early.

commonErrors.error: No one prepares for the rebound.
commonErrors.correction: Hold one connected outlet once immediate danger is controlled.

progressions: Increase the attacking numerical advantage.
Begin with a turnover closer to defensive 50.
Allow full-ground counterattack after the defensive exit.
Add a scoreboard scenario where conceding any score is costly.
Reduce the recovery delay but increase attacking speed.
regressions: Reduce the attacking team’s available space.
Pause after the turnover to identify recovery roles.
Use controlled movement rather than full-speed attack.
successIndicators: Recover through central and dangerous space.
Support the back line without overcrowding.
Provide an outlet after possession is won.
matchApplication: Midfielders are regularly caught ahead of the football when possession changes. This simulation develops the recovery patterns required to protect the back line, deny central access and support the next defensive possession.

title: Forward-Half Width Preservation Simulation
primarySkill: Maintaining attacking width while the football is retained in the forward half.
objective: Develop the forward group’s ability to preserve width, separate defenders and create usable scoring options while the football moves across the attacking half.
groundSize: From approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line, using the full width of the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark left, central and right attacking lanes.
Position forwards and defenders inside 50.
Position midfield ball carriers between 50 and 70 metres from goal.
Begin with possession on one side of the ground.
Require at least one forward to occupy the opposite-side lane.
The attacking team attempts to move the defence and create a high-quality shot.
The defending team attempts to intercept and exit through marked gates.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession on one forward flank.
Forwards organise leading, holding and opposite-side roles.
The ball carrier may enter immediately, retain possession or switch direction.
As the football moves, forwards adjust while preserving separation across the width of the ground.
The opposite-side forward remains available for a switch or long release.
Play continues until a score, defensive exit or stoppage.
Award three points for a goal.
Award two points for a mark created through an opposite-side switch.
Award one point for a controlled entry that produces a ground-level scoring opportunity.
Reset from the opposite flank.
coachingPoints: The far-side forward should not be drawn unnecessarily toward the football.
Leading players must maintain separate lanes and depths.
Central space should remain available for a timed lead.
Ball carriers should recognise when the opposition has over-shifted.
Opposite-side players must remain engaged and ready to move.
Deep forwards should avoid following high forwards out of scoring range.
Forward pressure must begin immediately if possession is lost.
Players outside 50 must maintain defensive protection.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Occupation of all three attacking lanes.
Separation between high and deep forwards.

commonErrors.error: All forwards move toward the ball side.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one or more players occupying the far-side lane.

commonErrors.error: Multiple forwards lead through the corridor simultaneously.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger central movements and preserve one clear lane.

commonErrors.error: Deep forwards follow high forwards too far.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a dangerous scoring target close to goal.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier ignores the opposite side.
commonErrors.correction: Scan across the full width before forcing an entry.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stop after an interception.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and deny the first exit.

progressions: Allow defenders to zone away from direct opponents.
Increase pressure on midfield ball carriers.
Require the attacking team to use both sides before scoring.
Continue play to the opposite goal after a defensive rebound.
Add a time limit for generating a shot.
regressions: Pause after each switch to correct spacing.
successIndicators: Preserve width across the forward half.
Create distinct high, deep and lateral options.
Generate entries to the forward’s advantage.
matchApplication: Forward lines often become congested when every attacker moves toward the football. This simulation develops the discipline required to maintain width, stretch defenders and create space for central or opposite-side scoring opportunities.
relatedDrills: MS-022 – Forward-Line Rotation After Turnover Simulation

title: Congestion Escape Handball Chain Simulation
primarySkill: Escaping a congested contest through coordinated handball support.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to secure a contested football, create layered handball support and escape congestion without transferring pressure to a teammate.
groundSize: A contested starting zone approximately 20 x 20 metres connected to a transition area 50–70 metres long.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark a congested contest square and three exit lanes.
Position equal numbers from both teams inside and around the square.
Place outside runners in each exit lane.
Begin with a ground ball, tackle release or stoppage.
The team winning possession attempts to escape through a handball chain.
The opposition attempts to trap the football or win turnover.
Rotate inside and outside roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach releases the football into the contested square.
Players compete to win or secure possession.
The first ball winner protects the football and identifies support.
Teammates create short, lateral and backward handball options.
The team attempts to complete two or three handballs before releasing to an outside runner.
The outside runner carries or kicks through an exit gate.
Award three points for a clean escape and controlled exit.
Award two points for escaping after absorbing a tackle.
Award the defending team three points for trapping the football or forcing a turnover.
Reset with different starting positions.
coachingPoints: The first possession must be secured before the release is attempted.
Support players should arrive at different angles and depths.
Handballs must move the football away from pressure, not sideways into pressure.
Players should communicate before entering the congestion.
The receiver should remain balanced and ready to continue the chain.
Outside runners must hold width until the football is released.
Players who dispose should block, shepherd or continue supporting.
If no clean release exists, players should protect the football and force a stoppage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Decision to escape or accept a stoppage.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner handballs immediately without control.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the football and identify a receiver first.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand directly behind each other.
commonErrors.correction: Create lateral, forward and backward angles.

commonErrors.error: Handballs transfer pressure to a teammate.
commonErrors.correction: Release toward space and the receiver’s safe side.

commonErrors.error: Outside runners enter congestion too early.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the football clearly exits.

commonErrors.error: Players force a release when trapped.
commonErrors.correction: Absorb contact and create a stoppage when no safe option exists.

progressions: Increase the number of pressure players.
Reduce the size of the contested square.
Allow full transition to goal after the escape.
Restrict the escape to the least defended gate.
Begin with the attacking team outnumbered inside the contest.
regressions: Pause after the first possession to organise support.
successIndicators: Accept a stoppage when escape is unsafe.
matchApplication: Congested football is rarely escaped by one disposal alone. This simulation develops the layered support and decision making required to move the football from a contested area into open transition.

title: Opposite-Wing Release Simulation
primarySkill: Releasing the opposite-side wing after drawing pressure to one side.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to retain an opposite-side wing option, transfer the football across the ground and use the released player to advance into attack.
groundSize: Defensive 50 to attacking 50 across the full width of the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark left and right wing channels and a central corridor.
Position one team in possession on a defensive or midfield wing.
Organise the opposition to pressure the ball side.
Position the opposite wing in the far-side channel.
Place high forwards and midfield support ahead of the opposite wing.
The possession team attempts to switch and release the far-side wing.
The defending team attempts to intercept or delay the switch.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins on one side of the ground.
Short and lateral possession is used to draw the opposition toward the football.
The opposite wing maintains width and adjusts depth.
When the switch is available, the football is transferred across the ground.
The opposite wing receives and attacks forward space.
Supporting midfielders and forwards connect to the released player.
Award three points for a switch that produces a controlled inside-50 entry.
Award two points for releasing the wing beyond the centre.
Award the defending team three points for intercepting the switch.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: The opposite wing must remain wide enough to stretch the defence.
The wing should adjust depth to remain a realistic kicking option.
Players near the football must move the opposition before switching.
The switch kick should travel to the receiver’s advantage side.
Support must arrive inside and ahead of the released wing.
The receiver should accelerate immediately if space is available.
The team must retain protection behind the football.
Communication should identify the far-side option early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Width and depth of the opposite wing.
Whether the opposition is moved before the switch.
Quality and placement of the switch kick.

commonErrors.error: The opposite wing moves too close to the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width and remain outside the opposition press.

commonErrors.error: The wing remains at a fixed depth.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust forward or backward to maintain a clear kicking lane.

commonErrors.error: The switch is attempted before the defence shifts.
commonErrors.correction: Use short possession to draw pressure first.

commonErrors.error: The receiver stops after marking.
commonErrors.correction: Play on when space and support are available.

commonErrors.error: No inside support follows the switch.
commonErrors.correction: Midfielders must connect inside and behind the released wing.

progressions: Allow the opposition to disguise its far-side coverage.
Reduce the time available after the switch.
Require the wing to create a shot or goal assist.
Continue full-ground play after a turnover.
Begin with the possession team under greater pressure.
regressions: Allow the opposite wing to begin unopposed.
Pause before the final switch kick.
successIndicators: Move the opposition toward the ball side.
Release the wing into forward space.
Provide immediate inside and forward support.
matchApplication: Opposite-side wings can become damaging attacking outlets when they maintain width while the opposition shifts toward the football. This simulation develops the patience and connection required to use that space effectively.

title: Post-Mark Movement Simulation
primarySkill: Creating immediate team movement after a player takes a mark.
objective: Develop both teams’ ability to reorganise immediately after a mark, with the possession team creating layered options and the defending team protecting the most dangerous next disposal.
groundSize: Half to two-thirds of a ground.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Divide players into attacking and defending teams across half to two-thirds of a ground.
Begin with one player taking a mark at a nominated field position.
Position teammates at realistic short, lateral, long and behind-support locations.
Position defenders to guard likely next options.
Mark a forward target zone.
Rotate the marking player and starting location.
Use both attacking and defensive-half marks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach delivers the football to a player who takes a mark.
As soon as the mark is completed, teammates begin their movement.
The possession team creates at least three options at different depths and angles.
The marking player decides whether to play on, kick short, switch, go long or hold.
Defenders protect the corridor and communicate likely receivers.
Play continues until the attacking team reaches the target zone, turns the football over or is forced out of bounds.
Award two points for creating three clear options within four seconds.
Award three points for reaching the target zone under control.
Award the defending team two points for denying forward movement.
Reset from a new mark location.
coachingPoints: Movement begins when the mark is taken, not when the umpire calls play on.
Options should exist at different depths and angles.
The nearest player should not automatically demand the football.
The ball carrier must scan before moving from the mark.
Behind-support should remain available when forward options are closed.
Defenders should guard dangerous space rather than following every short lead.
Players must anticipate the disposal after the next disposal.
Communication should identify play-on opportunities and pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed of movement after the mark.

commonErrors.error: Players wait until the ball carrier is ready to kick.
commonErrors.correction: Begin movement immediately when the mark is completed.

commonErrors.error: All options lead short.
commonErrors.correction: Create short, medium, long and behind options.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier plays on without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Check pressure and the next disposal before leaving the mark.

commonErrors.error: Players crowd the same side.
commonErrors.correction: Spread into separate angles and depths.

commonErrors.error: Defenders chase every receiver.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the corridor and highest-threat options first.

progressions: Reduce the time available after the mark.
Add full defensive pressure after the first disposal.
Include scoreboard scenarios requiring fast or slow play.
Remove marked starting positions.
Continue until a scoring shot is created.
regressions: Pause after the mark to identify options.
successIndicators: Create options at varied depths and angles.
Connect the first possession to the next phase.
matchApplication: Every mark creates a short period in which both teams reorganise. This simulation develops the movement habits required to use that time effectively rather than becoming static around the ball carrier.

title: Behind-the-Ball Defensive Roll Simulation
primarySkill: Rolling players behind the football as the team attacks.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to attack with sufficient numbers while maintaining connected defensive coverage behind the football.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Begin with one team attacking from half-back.
Identify two to four players responsible for maintaining behind-the-ball coverage.
Mark a reference line approximately 20 metres behind the football.
The attacking team attempts to score while maintaining connected coverage.
The opposition attempts to win possession and counterattack quickly.
Rotate behind-the-ball roles between defenders, wings and midfielders.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession at half-back.
As the football advances, selected players roll into positions behind or lateral to possession.
The team attacks through normal ball movement.
If possession is lost, the opposition counterattacks immediately.
Behind-the-ball players attempt to delay, intercept or direct the counterattack.
Award the attacking team three points for a goal.
Award one bonus point if the team retains correct behind-the-ball coverage at the moment of the forward entry.
Award the opposition three points for scoring from a turnover.
Stop after a score, defensive exit or 60 seconds.
Reset with different players responsible for coverage.
coachingPoints: Behind-the-ball coverage must move with possession rather than remain fixed.
Players should stay connected enough to influence a turnover.
Coverage should protect the corridor and likely rebound lanes.
The team must avoid leaving all defenders goal side but disconnected from midfield.
Players behind the football remain active attacking options.
Communication must identify who is holding, rolling or pressing forward.
After turnover, the nearest player pressures while others protect space.
Once possession is regained, coverage players should help relaunch the attack.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Position of players behind the football.
Distance between defensive coverage and attacking possession.
Contribution to the next attacking possession.

commonErrors.error: Coverage players remain too deep.
commonErrors.correction: Move with the football and stay close enough to influence turnover.

commonErrors.error: Everyone attacks forward of possession.
commonErrors.correction: Assign clear behind-the-ball responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Players guard opponents but leave the corridor open.
commonErrors.correction: Protect dangerous central space first.

commonErrors.error: Coverage roles are duplicated.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate who holds and who can advance.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after intercepting.
commonErrors.correction: Use the regain to relaunch the attack quickly.

progressions: Reduce the number of players allowed behind the football.
Increase opposition counterattack speed.
Add scoreboard scenarios requiring aggressive attack.
Remove the reference line.
Play a full quarter without coach interruption.
regressions: Increase the number of players assigned behind the football.
Pause before turnovers to check structure.
successIndicators: Protect the corridor and likely rebound lanes.
Remain involved in attacking ball movement.
matchApplication: Teams that commit numbers forward without maintaining coverage are vulnerable to damaging counterattacks. This simulation develops the balance required to attack aggressively while preserving defensive security.

title: Lead-Up-to-Deep Transition Simulation
primarySkill: Connecting a lead-up possession to a deeper attacking option.
objective: Develop the forward group’s ability to use a lead-up mark or possession to create and access a deeper scoring opportunity.
groundSize: From the centre square to the attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position midfielders near the centre and forwards at high, medium and deep starting positions.
Position defenders in realistic match-ups.
Begin with midfield possession under moderate pressure.
One forward presents as a lead-up target between the centre and 50-metre arc.
Deeper forwards react to the lead-up movement.
The attacking team attempts to connect the lead-up possession to a deeper mark or scoring opportunity.
Rotate lead-up and deep roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession near the centre.
A high forward presents into a clear lead-up lane.
Other forwards preserve or create space deeper inside 50.
If the lead-up player receives, nearby forwards initiate second-phase movement.
The lead-up player scans and delivers to the best deeper option.
Play continues until a score, defensive rebound or stoppage.
Award two points for a clean lead-up connection.
Award three points for a mark inside 30 metres created from that connection.
Award the defending team two points for an intercept and controlled exit.
Reset with altered forward positions.
coachingPoints: The lead-up forward should create a clear target without emptying the entire forward line.
Deep forwards must react after the lead-up movement, not copy it.
The lead-up receiver should arrive side-on and scan before possession.
Second-phase leads should begin as the football travels to the lead-up player.
Kicks must be placed to the deeper forward’s advantage.
Ground-level support should prepare beneath the deep contest.
Players outside 50 must protect against rebound.
Forward pressure begins immediately after a failed entry.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Body position of the lead-up receiver.

commonErrors.error: Multiple forwards lead toward midfield.
commonErrors.correction: Nominate one lead-up option and preserve deeper roles.

commonErrors.error: Deep forwards move too early.
commonErrors.correction: Begin second-phase movement as the first kick travels.

commonErrors.error: The lead-up receiver faces away from goal.
commonErrors.correction: Arrive side-on and scan before possession.

commonErrors.error: The final entry is rushed.
commonErrors.correction: Balance and identify the highest-percentage deeper option.

commonErrors.error: No support exists beneath the deep contest.
commonErrors.correction: Position ground-level forwards around the expected drop zone.

progressions: Increase pressure on the lead-up player.
Allow defenders to zone off opponents.
Remove preset forward roles.
Add a time limit for producing a shot.
Continue full-ground transition after a defensive rebound.
regressions: Pause after the lead-up mark to coach second-phase movement.
successIndicators: Deliver the football to the deeper forward’s advantage.
matchApplication: A lead-up possession is most effective when it connects directly to the next attacking layer. This simulation develops the coordinated movement required to use a high forward without sacrificing dangerous deep options.
relatedDrills: MS-022 – Forward-Line Rotation After Turnover Simulation

title: Rebound Support Triangle Simulation
primarySkill: Creating a three-player support structure after winning possession in defence.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to form a balanced support triangle around the first defensive possession and use it to escape pressure.
groundSize: Defensive 50 to approximately 20 metres beyond the arc.
coachingDifficulty: 3 – Intermediate organisation, rotations or several behaviours
setup:
Position defenders and opposition forwards inside defensive 50.
Mark central and wide exit gates.
Begin with an intercept, spoil or ground-ball win.
Require the two nearest teammates to create forward, lateral and behind support around the ball winner.
The opposition applies immediate forward pressure.
The defending team attempts to escape through a support triangle.
Rotate the starting ball winner and support roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach introduces the football into defensive 50.
A defender wins possession.
The two nearest teammates create separate support angles.
One option moves forward or outside, while another remains lateral or behind.
The ball winner selects the safest effective release.
The support triangle moves with the next possession.
Award three points for exiting defensive 50 with all three players connected.
Award two points for retaining possession through three disposals.
Award the attacking team three points for a turnover and score.
Reset with a different starting contest.
coachingPoints: Support players should not stand in the same line.
One option should reduce pressure while another creates forward movement.
The ball winner must scan before releasing.
The triangle should move with the football rather than disappear after one disposal.
Players should maintain enough separation to avoid one defender covering two options.
The behind option provides security if the forward lane closes.
At least one player must remain prepared for turnover defence.
Communication should identify pressure and the safest release.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Defensive reaction if possession is lost.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand directly behind each other.
commonErrors.correction: Create distinct forward, lateral and behind angles.

commonErrors.error: Both support players run forward.
commonErrors.correction: Keep one safe option behind or lateral to possession.

commonErrors.error: The triangle ends after one disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Move all three points with the football.

commonErrors.error: Players stand too close together.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough separation to stretch the pressure.

commonErrors.error: The ball winner releases without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Check all three options before disposing.

progressions: Increase opposition forward pressure.
Require the triangle to connect to a wing or midfielder.
Continue full-ground play after the exit.
Reduce the time available for the first disposal.
Begin with the defending team outnumbered.
regressions: Mark the three support positions with cones.
Pause after possession is won to organise the triangle.
successIndicators: Provide both attacking and safety options.
matchApplication: The first possession after a defensive win often fails because the ball carrier has only one obvious option. This simulation develops a simple, repeatable support structure that improves decision making and exit security.

title: Interchange and Positional Rotation Simulation
primarySkill: Maintaining team structure during interchange and positional rotations.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to complete interchange and positional rotations without leaving structural gaps, unguarded opponents or unclear responsibilities.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground with an interchange area marked.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams with interchange players available.
Mark a realistic interchange area.
Assign starting positions and potential rotation chains.
Prepare rotation cards such as wing-to-bench, half-forward-to-wing, midfielder-to-half-forward and defender-to-midfield.
Begin live match simulation.
Coaches call rotations at unpredictable times.
Players must communicate and complete the rotation while play continues.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams begin live play from a nominated restart.
The coach calls an interchange or positional rotation.
The outgoing player confirms the change with the incoming player or next positional replacement.
Players complete the rotation without leaving a role vacant.
Teammates adjust match-ups and team spacing.
Play continues throughout the rotation.
Award two points for completing the rotation without a structural error.
Award three points if the team retains possession or prevents a score during the change.
Deduct one point for an unguarded opponent, vacant role or interchange error.
Complete multiple rotations across different lines.
coachingPoints: The outgoing player must confirm who is replacing the role.
Rotations should occur through clear communication rather than assumption.
Players must understand both their new role and the role being vacated.
The nearest leader should identify any temporary structural gap.
Match-ups must be handed over before a player leaves the ground.
Incoming players should enter with immediate awareness of ball location and team shape.
Rotations should avoid moving several connected players simultaneously unless planned.
The team must remain focused on live play during the change.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Communication between outgoing and incoming players.
Awareness of the football during the rotation.

commonErrors.error: A player leaves before confirming the replacement.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the role handover before exiting.

commonErrors.error: Incoming players enter without knowing the ball location.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the ground and receive the role call before entering.

commonErrors.error: Multiple players assume someone else filled the role.
commonErrors.correction: Use a clear verbal confirmation from the replacement.

commonErrors.error: Match-ups are abandoned during rotation.
commonErrors.correction: Hand the opponent to a teammate before moving.

commonErrors.error: The team stops communicating after the change.
commonErrors.correction: Continue role and match-up calls until structure is stable.

progressions: Call multiple linked rotations.
Introduce rotations during high-pressure defensive phases.
Remove coach reminders and allow player leaders to manage rotations.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Include unexpected injury or blood-rule replacements.
regressions: Provide players with printed role cards.
successIndicators: Continue communicating until structure is restored.
matchApplication: Interchange and positional changes occur while the match continues. Poor communication can leave dangerous opponents unguarded or create temporary structural holes. This simulation develops a reliable process for completing rotations under live conditions.

title: Match-Simulation Movement and Connection Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating coordinated movement and connection across all match phases.
objective: Assess whether the team can independently apply the movement, support and structural connection principles developed throughout MS-021 to MS-039 during continuous match simulation.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with interchange players.
Prepare six starting scenarios covering defensive recovery, forward-half possession, congestion, wing switch, defensive rebound and positional rotation.
Assign coaches specific movement and connection behaviours to assess.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Play three blocks of eight to ten minutes.
Require player leaders to manage structural corrections between blocks.
Use minimal coach intervention during live play.
Begin each block from a different scenario.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the first starting scenario.
Teams organise and begin live play.
Once the initial phase is complete, play continues without restrictions.
Coaches assess movement before possession, support around the football, team spacing and reaction after turnovers.
Interchange or positional rotations are introduced during each block.
At the end of the block, teams complete a two-minute player-led review.
The next block begins from a different field position and scoreboard condition.
Award points for both the match score and nominated movement behaviours.
The final block is played with no advance warning of the starting challenge.
Conclude with team and individual ratings against the success indicators.
coachingPoints: Players must move before the football arrives.
Support should exist forward, lateral and behind possession.
Defensive recovery should protect dangerous space rather than simply follow opponents.
Forward width and depth must be preserved throughout ball movement.
Players should escape congestion by creating angles rather than crowding the contest.
The entire team must shift and reconnect as the football changes sides.
Behind-the-ball coverage should remain connected to the attack.
Rotations and interchanges must not create structural gaps.
Communication should occur before movement and role changes.
Coaches should assess repeated behaviour rather than isolated success.

commonErrors.error: Players move only when directly involved.
commonErrors.correction: Move to create space, support and defensive coverage for teammates.

commonErrors.error: Team shape becomes compressed around the football.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve width, depth and behind support.

commonErrors.error: Recovery runners follow opponents from behind.
commonErrors.correction: Run to dangerous space and regain goal-side influence.

commonErrors.error: Forward movement removes all deep options.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a balance between lead-up and scoring positions.

commonErrors.error: Interchange rotations create temporary gaps.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm replacements and match-up handovers before movement.

progressions: Play a full quarter without coach interruption.
Remove all field markers.
Add fatigue and interchange restrictions.
Introduce hidden tactical objectives for each team.
Record the simulation for detailed review.
regressions: Use four starting scenarios rather than six.
Keep visible lane and coverage markers.
Provide player leaders with structural reminder cards.
successIndicators: Preserve forward-half width and deep options.
Escape congestion through effective support angles.
Link lead-up and deeper forward movement.
Complete interchange and positional rotations safely.
Maintain team connection during continuous football.
matchApplication: This assessment completes the movement stage of the Match Simulation chapter. It determines whether players can combine off-ball movement, support, defensive recovery, forward spacing, switching, rebound structure and positional rotation during realistic, uninterrupted football.
relatedDrills: MS-033 – Congestion Escape Handball Chain Simulation
MS-039 – Interchange and Positional Rotation Simulation

title: Contested Centre-Bounce Recovery Simulation
primarySkill: Recovering team structure after an untidy or lost centre-bounce contest.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to respond when a centre-bounce contest does not produce clean possession, recover effective roles around the loose football and prevent the opposition from gaining an uncontested clearance.
groundSize: Centre square extending approximately 70 metres toward both goals.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position rucks and centre-square midfielders for both teams.
Add wings, half-forwards and half-backs outside the square.
Mark scoring gates approximately 50–70 metres in each direction.
Begin each repetition with an intentionally variable ball-up.
The ruck contest may produce a clean hit, neutral ball, misdirected hit or immediate secondary contest.
Both teams attack their nominated scoring end.
Rotate centre-square combinations every three repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach conducts a variable centre ball-up.
Players compete for first possession without knowing where the football will fall.
If clean possession is not established, players immediately reorganise around the secondary contest.
The nearest player attacks or pressures the football.
Teammates protect defensive-side space, create an outlet and track opposition receivers.
The team winning possession attempts to move through its scoring gate or produce a forward entry.
Award three points for a controlled clearance after winning a secondary contest.
Award two points for forcing a neutral stoppage after losing first possession.
Award one point for preventing the opposition from crossing its gate within ten seconds.
Reset after a score, stoppage, turnover or football out of bounds.
coachingPoints: Players must expect the ruck contest to produce an imperfect outcome.
The nearest player attacks the football while others organise around that action.
Defensive-side protection remains essential during a loose centre-square contest.
Players should avoid all entering the same ground-ball space.
One midfielder should remain available as the release option.
Wings must judge whether to hold width, support the contest or defend the opposition exit.
Communication should identify ball winner, pressure player and defensive-side responsibility.
The team must transition immediately once possession becomes clear.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Reaction to an unpredictable ruck outcome.
Separation between contest and support roles.
Availability of an outside or backward release.
Wing decisions around width and contest support.

commonErrors.error: All midfielders chase the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: Allocate contest, defensive-side and release roles.

commonErrors.error: Players assume the ruck hit will reach its target.
commonErrors.correction: Prepare for neutral, missed and opposition-directed outcomes.

commonErrors.error: The opposition’s outside receiver is left unguarded.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain awareness of dangerous release players.

commonErrors.error: Wings collapse before the contest outcome is clear.
