The next disposal should be identified before the transfer is completed.
Far-side width must remain available if the corridor closes.
Players behind the football must guard against a central turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the opposition is moved before corridor entry.
Position and angle of the central receiver.
Speed of the transfer and release.

commonErrors.error: The corridor is forced immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until central space is genuinely available.

commonErrors.error: The receiver stands flat and faces the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Lead at an angle and arrive side-on.

commonErrors.error: Support behind the football disappears.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain a safe outlet throughout the transfer.

commonErrors.error: The central receiver holds the football too long.
commonErrors.correction: Identify and execute the next option quickly.

commonErrors.error: Far-side players collapse toward the transfer.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve width as an alternative attacking route.

progressions: Reduce the central receiver’s disposal time.
Allow the defence to change between zone and man-on-man.
Require the transfer to produce a mark inside 30 metres.
Continue full-ground play after a central turnover.
Start with greater pressure on the wing possession.
successIndicators: Move the opposition before transferring centrally.
Enter the corridor without forcing risk.
Release the football before pressure closes.
matchApplication: Wide possession becomes more damaging when it can be transferred safely into the corridor. This simulation develops the judgement and movement required to shift from boundary control to direct attack.
relatedDrills: MS-013 – Corridor Access and Release Simulation

title: Midfield Line-Break Connection Simulation
primarySkill: Connecting possession through the midfield line to break opposition defensive structure.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to create and use a midfield receiver who can break a defensive line and connect the football to the forward half.
groundSize: From defensive 50 to attacking 50 across approximately two-thirds of a ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Mark three horizontal zones: defensive line, midfield line and forward line.
Position one team in possession in the defensive zone.
Position the opposition in a connected defensive shape across midfield.
Place midfield receivers between and beyond opposition lines.
Position high forwards and deeper forwards in the attacking zone.
The possession team attempts to break the midfield line through a controlled receiver.
The defending team attempts to force wide or backward possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins from defensive 50.
Players circulate the football to move the midfield defensive line.
Midfield receivers lead between opponents, beyond the line or laterally into space.
The ball carrier selects a receiver capable of turning or releasing forward.
Supporting runners move beyond and behind the receiver.
Play continues to a forward entry and scoring opportunity.
Award three points for a line-breaking possession followed by a shot.
Award two points for breaking the midfield line under control.
Award the defending team three points for intercepting the line-breaking disposal.
Reset from a different side and defensive structure.
coachingPoints: Midfield receivers must move across and between defensive lines.
Receivers should avoid standing directly behind opponents.
The ball carrier must assess the receiver’s body position and pressure.
A line break may be created through a kick, handball receive or run-and-carry.
Support must appear forward, lateral and behind the receiver.
High forwards should provide the next connection without crowding midfield space.
Players behind the football must protect against an intercept.
The team should accelerate after breaking the line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether receivers are visible to the ball carrier.
Support beyond and behind the line break.
Defensive balance after the attacking disposal.

commonErrors.error: Midfielders stand behind direct opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Lead across or away from the defender into visible space.

commonErrors.error: The receiver marks facing backward under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Arrive side-on or provide an immediate release option.

commonErrors.error: The line-breaking disposal is forced into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Move the defence and wait for the receiver to separate.

commonErrors.error: Support runners remain behind the play.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate beyond the receiver once the line is broken.

commonErrors.error: All defenders move ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected coverage against intercept turnover.

progressions: Increase pressure on midfield receivers.
Allow the opposition to change defensive line height.
Require the line break to produce a mark inside 30 metres.
Add a time limit for progressing from defence to attack.
Continue live play after turnovers.
regressions: Reduce the number of midfield defenders.
successIndicators: Receive in a position to continue forward.
Connect the line break to the forward structure.
matchApplication: Teams must connect through midfield to avoid becoming trapped in defensive possession or relying on repeated long contests. This simulation develops controlled progression through opposition lines.

title: Forward-Entry Recycle and Re-Attack Simulation
primarySkill: Recycling an ineffective forward entry and rebuilding another attacking opportunity.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to recover an incomplete or low-quality forward entry, retain possession outside 50 and rebuild a more effective attacking phase.
groundSize: From approximately 80 metres from goal to the goal line.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position attackers and defenders inside and around forward 50.
Position high forwards, wings and midfielders outside the arc.
Begin with an intentionally pressured or imperfect forward entry.
The attacking team attempts to recover the football or force it back outside 50.
Players outside 50 provide recycle and switch options.
The defensive team attempts to secure possession and exit.
Rotate starting entry locations and defensive structures.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with a pressured forward entry.
If the football is not marked cleanly, players contest the spill or defensive possession.
The attacking team attempts to regain possession or force a rushed exit.
Once possession is secured outside the immediate contest, the team may recycle backward or laterally.
Forwards reset their leading lanes and depth.
The team launches a second forward entry.
Award three points for a goal created from the recycled attack.
Award two points for a mark inside 30 metres after the recycle.
Award the defending team three points for a controlled exit.
Reset after a score, exit or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Players must recognise when the first forward entry has failed.
High forwards and midfielders should remain available outside the contest.
Backward possession should create a new angle rather than merely lose territory.
Forwards must reset their spacing before the second entry.
The opposite side should remain available for a switch.
Players should avoid forcing a second entry before the structure is ready.
The team must protect against a turnover during the recycle.
Forward pressure continues while the attacking shape resets.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Recognition of the failed first entry.
Purpose of backward or lateral possessions.
Speed and quality of the forward reset.

commonErrors.error: Players force the football back inside 50 immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and allow the forward structure to reset.

commonErrors.error: No support remains outside the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Keep high forwards and midfielders connected behind the entry.

commonErrors.error: Backward possession does not change the attacking angle.
commonErrors.correction: Shift the football laterally or to the opposite side.

commonErrors.error: Forwards continue leading into crowded space.
commonErrors.correction: Reset depth and create new separated lanes.

commonErrors.error: All players attack forward during the second entry.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain behind-the-ball coverage.

progressions: Increase defensive pressure after the recycle.
Require the second entry to come from the opposite side.
Add a time limit for rebuilding the attack.
Continue full-ground play after a defensive exit.
Introduce scoreboard scenarios requiring a goal.
regressions: Begin with the attacking team regaining the spill.
Pause before the second forward entry.
successIndicators: Identify when the first entry has failed.
matchApplication: Strong attacking teams do not force every incomplete entry back toward goal. They recover possession, move the defence and create another opportunity from a better angle.
relatedDrills: MS-053 – Ground-Level Forward Pressure Wave Simulation

title: Three-Line Ball-Movement Chain Simulation
primarySkill: Connecting defensive, midfield and forward lines through coordinated team ball movement.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move the football through all three positional lines while maintaining support, spacing and protection throughout the chain.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark defensive, midfield and forward zones.
Position one team in normal positional structure across the ground.
Organise the opposition in a connected defensive system.
Begin with controlled possession in the defensive zone.
The possession team attempts to connect through each line before scoring.
Players may rotate between lines when the movement creates space.
The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive line begins with possession.
Defenders create an exit and connect with a midfielder or high forward.
The midfield line receives and attempts to connect with the forward line.
Players behind the football continue supporting each possession.
Forwards organise an effective scoring entry.
If possession moves backward, all three lines adjust accordingly.
Award one point for a controlled defensive-to-midfield connection.
Award one point for a controlled midfield-to-forward connection.
Award three points for a goal completing the chain.
Reset after a score, turnover, defensive exit or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Each line must provide an option to the line behind and ahead.
Players should not become fixed within marked zones.
The first receiver in each line should know the next connection.
Support runners must continue after disposal.
Width and depth must be preserved across all three lines.
Players behind the football should remain close enough to influence turnover.
The team should accelerate when a defensive line is broken.
Communication must identify the next connection rather than only the current possession.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Width and depth across all three lines.

commonErrors.error: Lines become isolated from one another.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance between the nearest players in each line.

commonErrors.error: Players remain inside fixed zones.
commonErrors.correction: Rotate and move according to space and possession.

commonErrors.error: The receiver has no next option.
commonErrors.correction: Support ahead, lateral and behind before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after making a disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Continue into the next support or coverage position.

commonErrors.error: All defenders move ahead of possession.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected protection behind the football.

progressions: Remove the visible zone markers.
Increase opposition pressure.
Require the chain to be completed within a time limit.
Allow full contact and live counterattack.
Begin from different defensive restart types.
regressions: Nominate the first receiver in each zone.
successIndicators: Connect the defensive, midfield and forward lines.
Accelerate when a line is broken.
Retain defensive coverage throughout the chain.
matchApplication: Effective team ball movement requires connected positional lines. This simulation exposes gaps between defenders, midfielders and forwards and develops a complete possession chain from defence to score.

title: Defensive Rebound Switch-to-Score Simulation
primarySkill: Converting a defensive rebound and switch into a scoring opportunity.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to win possession in defence, transfer the football to the opposite side and complete a full scoring transition before the opposition can recover.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position one team in defensive structure inside defensive 50.
Position the opposition in forward-half attacking shape.
Begin with an intercept, spoil recovery or ground-ball win.
Organise far-side defenders, wing and midfielders as potential switch options.
Position forwards for transition at the opposite end.
The rebound team attempts to switch and score.
The opposition applies full transition defence.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins with an opposition forward entry.
The defending team wins possession.
Players assess whether the immediate side is blocked and whether a switch is available.
The football is transferred across the defensive half.
The opposite-side wing and midfielders accelerate into attacking space.
Forwards adjust their positions according to the speed and location of transition.
Award two points for completing the defensive switch.
Award three points for a controlled inside-50 entry after the switch.
Award five points for a goal completed from the rebound chain.
Reset after a score, turnover, stoppage or defensive exit.
coachingPoints: The defensive regain must be secured before switching.
Far-side movement should begin as possession is won.
The switch should move the opposition and create attacking space.
The opposite wing should maintain width and adjust depth.
Midfielders must connect inside and ahead of the released player.
Forwards should preserve depth until the rebound direction becomes clear.
Players behind the football must remain connected against another turnover.
The team should increase tempo once the switch releases space.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Speed and accuracy of the switch.

commonErrors.error: The switch begins before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete the mark or gather before changing direction.

commonErrors.error: Far-side players move too late.
commonErrors.correction: Start moving as soon as the defensive regain is likely.

commonErrors.error: The opposite wing receives without inside support.
commonErrors.correction: Midfielders must connect inside and ahead.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead before the rebound path is clear.
commonErrors.correction: Hold depth until the ball movement establishes direction.

commonErrors.error: Everyone runs forward after the switch.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected defenders and midfield coverage behind possession.

progressions: Increase opposition transition pressure.
Require the attacking chain to be completed within 20 seconds.
Begin with a contested defensive spoil.
Remove preset switch positions.
Continue live play after a turnover.
regressions: Begin with an uncontested intercept mark.
Allow the opposite wing to begin unopposed.
successIndicators: Adjust forward movement to the transition.
Generate a scoring opportunity while maintaining defensive balance.
matchApplication: Defensive rebounds become most damaging when they shift the opposition and attack the opposite side. This simulation links intercept defence, switching and full-ground scoring transition.

title: Half-Forward Outlet and Inside-50 Re-Entry Simulation
primarySkill: Using a half-forward outlet to retain possession and create a new inside-50 entry.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to use a half-forward outlet when direct access to goal is blocked and convert that possession into a better-positioned inside-50 re-entry.
groundSize: From the centre of the ground to the attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position midfield ball carriers approaching attacking 50.
Position defenders to deny direct central access.
Place high forwards on both flanks and deeper forwards inside 50.
Mark outlet zones near each half-forward flank.
The attacking team may use a half-forward outlet when the direct entry is closed.
The outlet receiver attempts to improve the entry angle or switch play.
The defending team attempts to intercept and exit.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession near the centre.
Defenders organise to deny a direct inside-50 entry.
A high forward presents into an outlet zone.
The ball carrier may use the outlet rather than force the football inside 50.
The outlet receiver scans for a deep lead, central option, overlap or switch.
Forwards reset and create a second entry pattern.
Award two points for a clean outlet possession.
Award three points for a mark inside 30 metres created from the outlet.
Award the defending team three points for an intercept and controlled exit.
Reset with altered defensive and outlet positioning.
coachingPoints: The outlet should provide a genuine change of angle.
High forwards must present without drawing every forward toward the football.
The receiver should arrive side-on and scan before possession.
Deep forwards should reset their leading patterns as the angle changes.
The opposite-side high forward should remain available for a switch.
Players outside 50 must remain connected behind the football.
The outlet receiver should not automatically kick inside 50.
Forward pressure begins immediately after turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing and angle of the outlet lead.
Movement of forwards after the angle changes.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces a direct entry into an outnumber.
commonErrors.correction: Use the half-forward outlet and rebuild the angle.

commonErrors.error: Multiple forwards lead into the outlet zone.
commonErrors.correction: Use one outlet while deeper players preserve space.

commonErrors.error: The outlet receiver marks facing away from goal.
commonErrors.correction: Lead at an angle and arrive side-on.

commonErrors.error: The receiver immediately kicks without scanning.
commonErrors.correction: Assess deep, central, switch and overlap options first.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after a defensive intercept.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate forward pressure and deny the exit.

progressions: Increase pressure on the outlet receiver.
Allow defenders to zone off direct opponents.
Require the re-entry to come from the opposite side.
Add a time limit for producing a shot.
Continue full-ground transition after a defensive exit.
regressions: Begin with the outlet receiver unopposed.
Increase the size of the outlet zones.
Pause after the outlet mark to coach forward movement.
successIndicators: Recognise when direct entry is unavailable.
Maintain pressure and protection after turnover.
matchApplication: Half-forward outlets allow teams to retain attacking possession and avoid low-percentage entries. This simulation develops the connection between midfield possession, high forwards and deeper scoring targets.
relatedDrills: MS-064 – Forward-Entry Recycle and Re-Attack Simulation

title: Behind-the-Ball Launch Simulation
primarySkill: Using players positioned behind the football to relaunch an attacking phase.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to use connected players behind possession to secure a loose or backward football, change the attacking angle and relaunch forward movement.
groundSize: From defensive 50 to attacking 50 across approximately two-thirds of a ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position one team in attacking possession through midfield.
Assign two to four players behind the football as connected coverage.
Position the opposition to apply pressure and create possible turnovers.
Begin with an attacking chain toward forward 50.
The coach may create a spoil, backward handball, loose football or partial turnover.
Behind-the-ball players attempt to secure possession and relaunch.
Rotate coverage roles between defenders, wings and midfielders.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins moving the football forward.
Players behind possession adjust with the attack.
The coach or opposition creates an incomplete possession or loose football.
Behind-the-ball players compete to secure the football.
Once possession is regained, they select a switch, forward release or supporting handball.
The team rebuilds its attacking shape and re-enters the forward half.
Award two points for securing the loose football.
Award three points for relaunching into a controlled forward entry.
Award the opposition three points for winning the loose football and counterattacking.
Reset with different coverage players and turnover locations.
coachingPoints: Players behind the football must remain close enough to influence the next contest.
Coverage positions should protect the corridor and likely spill locations.
Behind-the-ball players remain active possession options.
The first regain should secure control rather than force immediate attack.
The team should change the attacking angle when the original route has closed.
Forwards must reset after the relaunch.
Other players should spread as soon as possession is secured.
Communication should identify who attacks the loose football and who protects behind.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Distance between coverage players and possession.
Forward reset after possession is recovered.
Remaining coverage against a second turnover.

commonErrors.error: Coverage players remain too deep to influence the spill.
commonErrors.correction: Move with possession and maintain connection.

commonErrors.error: All coverage players attack the loose football.
commonErrors.correction: One contests while others protect space and support the next disposal.

commonErrors.error: The regain is kicked forward immediately without control.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and assess the new attacking angle.

commonErrors.error: Forwards continue old leading patterns.
commonErrors.correction: Reset movement according to the relaunch location.

commonErrors.error: Everyone moves forward after the regain.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain one connected layer behind possession.

progressions: Increase pressure around the loose football.
Create multiple incomplete possessions in one repetition.
Continue play to a full scoring outcome.
Reduce the number of coverage players.
Add a scoreboard scenario requiring aggressive attack.
regressions: Increase the number of coverage players.
Pause after the regain to organise the relaunch.
successIndicators: Maintain connected positions behind the football.
matchApplication: Players behind the football are not only defensive protection. They can recover incomplete attacks, retain possession and relaunch the team from a stronger angle.
relatedDrills: MS-064 – Forward-Entry Recycle and Re-Attack Simulation

title: Multi-Phase Team Communication Simulation
primarySkill: Maintaining clear team communication across changing match phases.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to communicate possession status, structure, threats and tactical priorities as play changes between stoppage, possession, turnover and scoring phases.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Assign line leaders for defence, midfield and attack.
Prepare restarts and scenarios involving possession, turnover, stoppage and scoreboard changes.
Assign coaches to observe communication categories.
Use live match simulation with minimal coach direction.
Require players to organise roles and tactical adjustments.
Rotate leadership responsibilities between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a nominated restart.
Players communicate match-ups, space, pressure and possession options.
When possession changes, teams must immediately communicate new attacking and defensive roles.
At stoppages, leaders call structure, score, time and intended plan.
During possession chains, players identify pressure, switch, corridor and support options.
Coaches introduce new scoreboard or time information during play.
Award one point for each clearly observed communication behaviour that changes or improves an action.
Award normal match points for scoring.
Complete three playing blocks of five to seven minutes.
Review which communication calls were useful, late, unclear or absent.
coachingPoints: Communication must be early enough to influence the action.
Calls should be short, specific and relevant.
Players should identify both danger and opportunity.
The team must communicate possession changes immediately.
Leaders should organise without dominating every decision.
Stoppage calls must include roles rather than only general encouragement.
Players away from the football often have the clearest information.
Communication should continue through fatigue and scoreboard pressure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Communication from players away from the football.

commonErrors.error: Calls occur after the action has happened.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate as the situation develops.

commonErrors.error: Players use vague calls such as “man up”.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the player, space or specific role.

commonErrors.error: Only one or two leaders communicate.
commonErrors.correction: Require information from all lines and nearby players.

commonErrors.error: Communication stops during fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Increase calls when physical capacity and concentration decline.

commonErrors.error: Players call constantly without useful information.
commonErrors.correction: Prioritise pressure, threats, options and role changes.

progressions: Remove coach communication entirely.
Conceal scoreboard information from some players.
Rotate leaders every two minutes.
Add crowd noise or controlled distractions.
Play a full quarter and assess communication trends.
regressions: Use one communication focus per block.
Pause at stoppages to organise calls.
Provide players with approved cue examples.
Reduce ground size and player numbers.
successIndicators: Continue communication under fatigue and pressure.
matchApplication: Team structure depends on information being shared quickly across the ground. This simulation assesses whether communication supports actual decisions and movement rather than functioning only as encouragement.
relatedDrills: MS-009 – Coach Observation and Feedback Simulation

title: Team Ball Movement Phase Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating structured team ball movement across defensive, midfield and attacking phases.
objective: Assess whether the team can independently apply the structured ball-movement principles developed in MS-061 to MS-069 during continuous and changing match situations.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with interchange players.
Prepare scenario cards covering defensive possession, wing possession, midfield line breaks, forward-half recycling and defensive rebound.
Assign coaches to assess specific ball-movement behaviours.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Play three blocks of ten to twelve minutes.
Use minimal coach intervention during live play.
Require player leaders to conduct short reviews between blocks.
Begin each block from a different field position and possession state.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the first starting scenario.
Teams organise and begin live play.
After the initial phase, play continues without restrictions.
Coaches assess spacing, support, line connection, tempo, decision making and turnover protection.
At selected stoppages, the coach may introduce a new starting position or scoreboard condition.
Teams must adapt their ball-movement method to the scenario.
At the end of each block, players complete a two-minute review.
Award points for normal scoring and nominated ball-movement behaviours.
The final block is played without advance notice of the starting tactical challenge.
Conclude with individual, line and team ratings against the success indicators.
coachingPoints: Defensive possession must create a clear launch rather than become static.
Wide possession should create corridor or opposite-side access.
Midfield receivers must move between defensive lines.
Failed entries should be recycled rather than forced.
Defensive, midfield and forward lines must remain connected.
Rebound switches should release opposite-side runners.
Half-forward outlets should improve the next entry.
Players behind the football must support relaunch and turnover protection.
Communication must identify phase, options and threats.
Coaches should assess repeatable team methods rather than isolated successful disposals.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Connection across all three positional lines.

commonErrors.error: Possession becomes slow without moving the opposition.
commonErrors.correction: Use each disposal to change angle, side or defensive positioning.

commonErrors.error: Team lines become disconnected.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain support between defenders, midfielders and forwards.

commonErrors.error: Players force central or forward options.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession and create the option before using it.

commonErrors.error: Failed entries are returned immediately to congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Recycle, reset the forward structure and re-enter from a better angle.

commonErrors.error: All support moves ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected possession and defensive coverage behind the ball.

progressions: Play a full quarter without coach interruption.
Remove all visual field markers.
Use hidden tactical objectives for each team.
Reduce interchange availability.
Record the assessment for detailed tactical review.
regressions: Use four starting scenarios rather than five.
Keep visible lane and zone markers.
Provide player leaders with ball-movement reminder cards.
successIndicators: Transfer safely from wide to central space.
Connect defensive, midfield and forward lines.
Convert defensive rebounds into attacking chains.
Relaunch through players behind the football.
Communicate phase changes and available options.
Perform team ball movement without continuous coach direction.
matchApplication: This assessment completes the first team-ball-movement stage of the Match Simulation chapter. It determines whether players can combine defensive launches, line connection, corridor access, recycling, switching and forward connection within continuous Australian football.
relatedDrills: MS-067 – Half-Forward Outlet and Inside-50 Re-Entry Simulation

title: Defensive-50 Overload-to-Release Simulation
primarySkill: Creating and using a numerical overload to escape defensive 50.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to create a temporary numerical advantage around defensive possession, draw opposition pressure and release the football into open space.
groundSize: Defensive goal line to approximately 25 metres beyond defensive 50.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one team in possession inside defensive 50.
Organise the opposition in a forward-half press.
Mark one overload zone on the starting side and three exit gates beyond defensive 50.
Allow the possession team one additional player inside the overload zone.
Position far-side defenders, wings and midfielders as release options.
Begin each repetition with a mark, free kick or controlled ground-ball possession.
Rotate the overload side and initial ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive team begins with possession inside the overload zone.
Nearby teammates create short and lateral options to attract opposition pressure.
The possession team attempts to involve the spare player without becoming crowded.
Once the opposition commits numbers, the ball carrier releases to the far side, corridor or advancing wing.
The team attempts to exit defensive 50 through a designated gate.
Award three points for a central exit created from the overload.
Award two points for a controlled wide exit.
Award the pressing team three points for a turnover and scoring opportunity.
Continue until an exit, turnover, score or stoppage.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: The overload should create an extra option rather than extra congestion.
Players must maintain different depths and angles.
The ball carrier should draw pressure before releasing.
The spare player should be positioned where one defender cannot cover two options.
The far-side release must remain available.
Players should accelerate once the press has been displaced.
Support behind the football must remain connected.
Communication should identify the spare player and the intended release side.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the overload creates usable space.
Support after the first exit possession.

commonErrors.error: Too many players enter the overload zone.
commonErrors.correction: Use only the numbers required to create one clear spare.

commonErrors.error: Players stand at the same depth.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger short, lateral and long options.

commonErrors.error: The football is released before the press commits.
commonErrors.correction: Draw an opponent before transferring possession.

commonErrors.error: The far side moves toward the overload.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain width until the release begins.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after escaping the first pressure line.
commonErrors.correction: Continue supporting until the football has exited defensive 50.

progressions: Remove the numerical advantage after the first disposal.
Allow the opposition to change pressing structures.
Continue play to the opposite goal.
Introduce a six-second decision limit.
Begin with the possession team under immediate physical pressure.
regressions: Increase the possession team’s overload to two spare players.
Pause after the first possession to organise spacing.
successIndicators: Maintain effective spacing around the overload.
matchApplication: Defensive teams often create exits by bringing an extra player to the ball side, attracting pressure and releasing the football elsewhere. This simulation develops the spacing and decision making required to use that advantage effectively.

title: Midfield Possession-to-Forward Isolation Simulation
primarySkill: Using controlled midfield possession to create an isolated forward contest.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move the opposition through midfield possession and create a favourable one-on-one or isolated forward contest.
groundSize: From the centre square to the attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position midfielders around the centre and attacking side of the ground.
Position forwards and defenders inside 50.
Mark two potential isolation areas inside attacking 50.
Begin with controlled midfield possession.
The attacking team attempts to move the defence and create a favourable isolated contest.
Other forwards must clear or hold space without becoming inactive.
The defending team attempts to prevent isolation and rebound.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession through midfield.
Players move the football laterally or backward to shift the defensive structure.
Forwards communicate which match-up or space is being isolated.
Supporting forwards clear the selected area and position for the likely spill.
The ball carrier delivers to the isolated forward when the advantage is established.
Play continues until a score, defensive rebound or stoppage.
Award three points for a mark inside the isolation area.
Award four points for a goal from the isolated contest.
Award the defending team three points for an intercept and controlled exit.
Reset with a different forward or isolation side.
coachingPoints: The team should create the isolation rather than announce it too early.
Midfield possession must move the defence away from the target area.
The selected forward should maintain separation from the defender.
Other forwards must clear space while remaining ready for ground-level support.
The kick should favour the forward’s protected side.
The ball carrier must recognise when the defence has recovered and avoid forcing the contest.
Midfielders must remain connected outside 50 against rebound.
Forward pressure begins immediately if the contest is lost.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether midfield possession moves the defence.
Separation between the isolated forward and other attackers.

commonErrors.error: The forward line clears too early.
commonErrors.correction: Create the isolation as the midfield possession develops.

commonErrors.error: Supporting forwards leave no ground-level coverage.
commonErrors.correction: Clear the marking space but remain connected to the spill.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces the entry after the defence recovers.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession and create another attacking option.

commonErrors.error: The kick favours the defender.
commonErrors.correction: Place the football to the forward’s protected side.

commonErrors.error: Midfielders all move forward of the entry.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain coverage outside 50 against rebound.

progressions: Allow defenders to zone off their direct opponents.
Change the isolated forward during the possession chain.
Add greater midfield pressure.
Require the isolated possession to produce a goal.
Continue full-ground play after a defensive rebound.
regressions: Begin with the forward already isolated.
successIndicators: Move the opposition before entering forward 50.
matchApplication: Teams can create high-quality scoring opportunities by moving the defence and isolating a favourable forward match-up. This simulation develops the complete process rather than simply practising one-on-one forward contests.
relatedDrills: MS-067 – Half-Forward Outlet and Inside-50 Re-Entry Simulation
MS-064 – Forward-Entry Recycle and Re-Attack Simulation

title: Boundary Compression-to-Open-Side Release Simulation
primarySkill: Escaping boundary congestion by transferring possession to the open side.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to draw opposition numbers toward a boundary contest, secure possession and transfer the football to open space on the opposite side.
groundSize: A boundary channel connected to the full opposite half of the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Begin with a boundary contest involving several players from both teams.
Position open-side wings, defenders and midfielders away from the congestion.
Mark one central and one wide open-side release gate.
The possession team attempts to secure the football and transfer away from the boundary.
The defending team attempts to trap possession or intercept the switch.
Rotate boundary and open-side roles.
Vary the starting field position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach starts a live boundary contest or throw-in.
Both teams compete for possession.
The team winning the football creates a short release away from immediate pressure.
Open-side players maintain width and adjust their depth.
The football is transferred through a kick, handball chain or switch possession.
The receiving player attacks through an open-side gate.
Award three points for a controlled open-side release.
Award two points for escaping the boundary through the corridor.
Award the defending team three points for trapping the football or intercepting the transfer.
Reset from a different boundary location.
coachingPoints: The first possession should escape immediate pressure rather than force a long switch.
Open-side players must remain available and visible.
Support around the contest should create a release angle.
The team should move the football quickly once the open side becomes available.
The switch kick must favour the receiver.
Players behind possession must protect against an intercepted transfer.
The far-side receiver should scan before the football arrives.
A repeat boundary stoppage remains acceptable when no safe release exists.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Release support around the boundary contest.
Width and depth of open-side players.
Timing and accuracy of the transfer.

commonErrors.error: The first possession attempts a long switch under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Create a short release before transferring the football.

commonErrors.error: Open-side players move toward the congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until possession is secured.

commonErrors.error: Support players stand directly behind the ball winner.
commonErrors.correction: Create lateral and backward release angles.

commonErrors.error: The switch hangs in the air and allows recovery.
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter, accurate kick to the receiver’s advantage.

commonErrors.error: Players force the release when trapped.
commonErrors.correction: Protect possession and accept the stoppage.

progressions: Reduce the space available around the boundary contest.
Add a recovering defender on the open side.
Continue the release to a full scoring opportunity.
Introduce scoreboard scenarios where territory is critical.
Begin with the possession team outnumbered at the contest.
regressions: Use controlled contact at the boundary contest.
successIndicators: Secure or neutralise the boundary contest.
Create an initial release from congestion.
Attack the open side at speed.
matchApplication: Boundary contests often draw most players toward one side of the ground. Teams that secure possession and access the opposite side can attack before the opposition recovers.

title: Full-Ground Overlap Chain Simulation
primarySkill: Creating and sustaining overlap support across multiple lines of the ground.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to create consecutive overlap runs from defence through midfield and into attack while preserving support behind the football.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position one team in defensive possession.
Organise opposition pressure across defensive, midfield and forward lines.
Place potential overlap runners behind and lateral to the initial ball carrier.
Position midfielders and forwards to continue the overlap chain.
Begin with an intercept or controlled defensive possession.
The attacking team attempts to complete at least three connected overlap actions.
The opposition attempts to delay, intercept or counterattack.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defensive team begins with possession.
The first overlap runner moves past or outside the ball carrier.
The ball carrier draws pressure and releases.
The receiving player connects with the next overlap or forward option.
Additional runners join from midfield and half-forward.
The team attempts to create a scoring opportunity.
Award one point for each successful overlap action.
Award three points for a controlled inside-50 entry.
Award five points for a goal following three or more overlaps.
Reset after a score, turnover, stoppage or defensive exit.
coachingPoints: Overlap runners should attack space rather than run directly beside the ball carrier.
The ball carrier must draw an opponent before releasing.
Runners should stagger their timing.
Players who dispose must continue supporting the chain.
A kicking option should remain available when handball pressure becomes excessive.
Support behind the football must remain connected.
Forwards should respond to the speed and direction of the overlap.
After turnover, runners must recover through the corridor.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Angles and timing of overlap runs.
Whether the ball carrier draws pressure.

commonErrors.error: Overlap runners move too close to the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Run wider or beyond to create separation.

commonErrors.error: Multiple runners arrive simultaneously.
commonErrors.correction: Stagger the first, second and third overlap efforts.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier releases before pressure commits.
commonErrors.correction: Carry directly at the defender before disposing.

commonErrors.error: The chain relies only on handball.
commonErrors.correction: Retain kicking options when the defence compresses.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after giving the football.
commonErrors.correction: Continue to the next support or coverage position.

progressions: Increase defender numbers.
Require the final entry to produce a goal.
Begin with the attacking team under immediate pressure.
Allow full contact and live counterattack.
Add a second transition immediately after a turnover.
regressions: Predetermine the first two overlap runners.
successIndicators: Create overlap support across multiple lines.
Connect the overlap to a scoring opportunity.
matchApplication: Damaging transition often requires several overlap efforts rather than one isolated run. This simulation develops continuous support from defence to attack.

title: Forward-Half Possession Lock and Switch Simulation
primarySkill: Retaining forward-half possession and switching the point of attack.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to retain possession outside attacking 50, prevent a defensive rebound and switch the point of attack to create a better scoring entry.
groundSize: Attacking half of the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position one team in forward-half possession.
Position defenders inside 50 and through the defensive exit lanes.
Mark wide possession zones outside attacking 50.
Begin with the football on one flank.
The attacking team attempts to retain possession, move the defence and switch the entry side.
Forwards reset their structure as the football changes sides.
The defending team attempts to intercept and exit beyond the centre line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession outside 50 on one side.
Players create short, lateral, backward and opposite-side options.
The team moves the football until the defence over-shifts or an entry opens.
The football may be switched to the opposite flank.
Forwards reset their leading patterns and depth.
Play continues to a scoring opportunity.
Award two points for retaining possession through a successful switch.
Award three points for a mark inside 30 metres after the switch.
Award the defending team three points for a controlled exit.
Reset from the opposite side.
coachingPoints: Possession should move the defensive structure.
Backward movement must create a new angle.
The opposite flank must remain occupied.
Forwards should reset rather than continue leading toward the old ball position.
Players outside 50 must remain connected against rebound.
The entry should occur only when the forward structure is ready.
The team should increase tempo after the switch.
Forward pressure begins immediately after turnover.

commonErrors.error: The team circulates without moving the defence.
commonErrors.correction: Change side, angle or depth with each possession.

commonErrors.error: Opposite-side players collapse toward the football.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the switch is available.

commonErrors.error: Forwards continue old leading patterns.
commonErrors.correction: Reset according to the new entry angle.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier enters before the forward line is ready.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until separated options appear.

commonErrors.error: Players outside 50 move too far forward.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected rebound protection.

progressions: Increase defensive pressure outside 50.
Require the attacking team to use both sides before scoring.
Add a time limit for creating a shot.
Continue full-ground transition after a defensive win.
Introduce scoreboard scenarios requiring possession retention.
regressions: Pause after the switch to coach forward reset.
successIndicators: Reset forward spacing after the switch.
Prevent or respond to defensive rebound.
matchApplication: Teams can maintain forward-half pressure without forcing repeated entries. This simulation develops controlled possession and point-of-attack changes around attacking 50.
relatedDrills: MS-064 – Forward-Entry Recycle and Re-Attack Simulation
MS-067 – Half-Forward Outlet and Inside-50 Re-Entry Simulation

title: Defensive Line-Break Prevention and Rebound Simulation
primarySkill: Preventing opposition line-breaking possession and launching a rebound after an intercept.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to deny central line-breaking options, intercept or pressure the possession and transition immediately into attack.
groundSize: From defensive 50 to the centre of the ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position the attacking team in possession across midfield and half-forward.
Organise the defending team in two connected defensive lines.
Mark central line-breaking channels and wide rebound gates.
Attackers attempt to find receivers between or beyond the defensive lines.
Defenders attempt to deny or intercept those possessions.
On turnover, the defending team immediately attacks through a rebound gate.
Rotate defensive lines and starting ball positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with controlled possession.
Attackers attempt to create a line-breaking receiver.
Defenders shift with the football and protect central space.
If a line-breaking disposal is attempted, defenders pressure, spoil or intercept.
On possession regain, the defending team spreads immediately.
The rebound continues through a wide or central gate.
Award the attacking team three points for a controlled line break followed by a shot.
Award the defending team two points for denying the line break.
Award three defensive points for an intercept and controlled rebound.
Reset after a score, rebound exit or stoppage.
coachingPoints: Defenders must maintain connection between lines.
Central receivers should be passed between defenders when they move through zones.
Players should see both the football and dangerous opponents.
The nearest defender pressures while others protect the next line.
Intercept opportunities should be taken only when coverage exists behind.
On regain, players must spread immediately.
The first rebound possession should reduce pressure.
Communication must identify line-break threats and handovers.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Quality of the first possession after regain.

commonErrors.error: Defensive lines separate too far.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance between midfield and defensive units.

commonErrors.error: Defenders follow opponents and expose central space.
commonErrors.correction: Hand over low-threat movement and protect the line.

commonErrors.error: Players watch only the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain vision of nearby receivers and dangerous space.

commonErrors.error: A defender intercepts without coverage behind.
commonErrors.correction: Attack the football only when a teammate protects the vacated space.

commonErrors.error: The team remains compressed after winning possession.
commonErrors.correction: Spread immediately into rebound options.

progressions: Increase attacking ball speed.
Remove visible line markers.
Allow full-ground counterattack after the regain.
Add a scoreboard scenario requiring aggressive rebound.
Reduce the number of defenders protecting each line.
successIndicators: Spread quickly after possession is regained.
Convert defensive work into controlled rebound.
matchApplication: Strong team defence denies possession between lines and turns interceptions into attacking opportunities. This simulation connects defensive structure directly to rebound football.

title: Centre-Square-to-Wing Connection Simulation
primarySkill: Connecting centre-square possession to a wing or outside runner.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to win or secure centre-square possession and release the football to an outside runner who can advance the attack.
groundSize: Centre square to one attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position rucks and midfielders inside the centre square.
Position wings and outside midfielders beyond the square.
Position half-forwards, forwards and defenders toward the attacking goal.
Begin each repetition with a centre ball-up.
The team winning possession attempts to connect with a wing or outside runner.
The defending team attempts to close the release and counterattack.
Rotate midfield and wing combinations.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach conducts a centre ball-up.
Players compete for first possession.
The ball winner or first receiver attempts to release to a wing or outside midfielder.
Wings hold width until the football exits the centre square.
The outside receiver attacks forward and connects with the forward line.
Play continues until a score, turnover or defensive exit.
Award two points for a clean centre-square-to-wing connection.
Award three points for a controlled inside-50 entry.
Award four points for a goal from the chain.
Reset with a different ruck and midfield setup.
coachingPoints: Wings must hold width until the clearance direction is clear.
Inside midfielders should protect the football and create an outside release.
The first handball or kick should lead the wing into space.
The wing should scan before possession arrives.
Supporting midfielders should continue running inside and behind the receiver.
Forwards should respond to the outside entry angle.
Players behind the clearance must protect against turnover.
Communication should identify the intended release side.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing and placement of the release.
Forward movement in response to the angle.

commonErrors.error: Wings collapse into the centre-square contest.
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until possession clearly exits.

commonErrors.error: Inside players force a release without control.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and create a clear handball or kick.

commonErrors.error: The disposal forces the wing to stop.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the receiver into forward space.

commonErrors.error: No support runs inside the wing.
commonErrors.correction: Midfielders must connect inside and behind the receiver.

commonErrors.error: Forwards maintain a central-only leading pattern.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust movement to the outside entry angle.

progressions: Allow the opposition wing to start closer to the release player.
Change the intended release side after the ball-up.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Continue full-ground play after turnover.
Require the wing to create a direct scoring assist.
regressions: Pause after first possession to identify the outside option.
successIndicators: Connect the outside receiver to the forward line.
matchApplication: Centre clearances are more effective when inside possession connects with outside runners. This simulation develops the relationship between centre-square players, wings and the forward structure.

title: Inside-50 Possession Retention and Shot Creation Simulation
primarySkill: Retaining possession inside attacking 50 until a high-quality shot becomes available.
objective: Develop the forward group’s ability to retain attacking possession, resist low-percentage shots and create a higher-quality scoring opportunity.
groundSize: Inside attacking 50.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Position forwards and defenders inside attacking 50.
Mark high-quality shot zones inside approximately 30 metres.
Begin with attacking possession in a pocket, flank or congested area.
Position support players around and behind the football.
The attacking team attempts to retain possession and create a shot from a high-quality zone.
The defending team attempts to intercept and exit.
Rotate starting locations and possession players.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession inside 50.
The ball carrier assesses whether an immediate shot is appropriate.
If the shot is low percentage, players create short, lateral or backward options.
Forwards reposition to open a higher-value scoring area.
The attacking team may handball, short kick, switch or centre the football.
Play continues until a shot, turnover or stoppage.
Award one point for a shot outside the high-quality zones.
Award three points for creating a shot inside a high-quality zone.
Award four points for a goal from that zone.
Award the defending team three points for a controlled exit.
coachingPoints: Players must distinguish between an available shot and a high-quality shot.
Short possession should improve the scoring angle.
Forwards should move defenders away from the desired scoring area.
Players behind the ball carrier must remain available.
The goal square should not become overcrowded.
The ball carrier must avoid centring blindly into an outnumber.
After turnover, forwards must apply immediate pressure.
Decision making should remain composed despite the proximity to goal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Movement to improve the scoring angle.
Availability of support around the ball carrier.
Occupation of the goal square and central space.

commonErrors.error: Players take the first available shot.
commonErrors.correction: Assess angle, pressure and teammate positioning first.

commonErrors.error: Short possession does not improve the opportunity.
commonErrors.correction: Use each disposal to move the defence or improve the angle.

commonErrors.error: Forwards crowd the goal square.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separation and clear space for the next receiver.

commonErrors.error: The ball is centred blindly.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm a teammate has advantage before using the central option.

commonErrors.error: Players stop after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate pressure and close the first exit.

progressions: Reduce the time available to create the shot.
Increase defender numbers.
Require the final shot to be taken from a nominated central zone.
Continue full-ground play after a defensive exit.
Introduce a scoreboard scenario requiring a goal.
regressions: Increase the size of the high-quality shot zones.
Begin with an unpressured ball carrier.
Pause to identify the best scoring area.
successIndicators: Assess the quality of the initial shot.
Move defenders and improve the scoring angle.
matchApplication: Forward efficiency improves when players resist low-percentage attempts and create better shots through short possession, movement and composure.
relatedDrills: MS-064 – Forward-Entry Recycle and Re-Attack Simulation
MS-067 – Half-Forward Outlet and Inside-50 Re-Entry Simulation
MS-075 – Forward-Half Possession Lock and Switch Simulation

title: Full-Ground Tempo Change Simulation
primarySkill: Changing team ball-movement tempo according to pressure, space and match context.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move between controlled possession and rapid attack according to the opposition structure, field position and scoreboard situation.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Prepare tempo cards including retain, move the defence, accelerate, gain territory and protect the lead.
Begin from defensive, midfield and forward-half possession.
Coaches may display or call a tempo instruction during play.
Teams must adjust collectively.
Rotate leadership responsibility between lines.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a nominated restart or controlled possession.
The team in possession uses the current tempo instruction.
During play, the coach changes the required tempo.
Players must communicate and adjust their movement, disposal selection and risk.
The opposition continues to defend and counterattack normally.
Tempo may change several times within one possession chain.
Award one behaviour point for each correct collective tempo adjustment.
Award normal match points for scoring.
Complete three blocks of five to seven minutes.
Review whether tempo changes improved or damaged the team’s position.
coachingPoints: Tempo change must involve the whole team.
Controlled possession should move the opposition and preserve safety.
Acceleration should occur when the defence loses shape.
Players should avoid increasing speed when support is absent.
Slowing play does not mean becoming stationary.
Score, time and field position should influence risk.
Communication must identify the tempo change early.
Players behind the football must adjust with the attacking speed.

commonErrors.error: Only the ball carrier changes tempo.
commonErrors.correction: All lines must adjust their movement and spacing.

commonErrors.error: Controlled possession becomes static.
commonErrors.correction: Continue creating angles and moving the opposition.

commonErrors.error: Players accelerate without forward support.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm runners and targets are available first.

commonErrors.error: The team continues fast play after the defence recovers.
commonErrors.correction: Return to control and rebuild the attacking shape.

commonErrors.error: Tempo changes are not communicated.
commonErrors.correction: Leaders must call the change before the next possession.

progressions: Remove coach tempo cards and require players to select the tempo.
Conceal scoreboard information from selected players.
Add final-minute scenarios.
Reduce interchange availability.
Play a full quarter with player-led tempo management.
regressions: Use only controlled and fast tempo instructions.
Reduce player numbers and ground size.
Pause to discuss the correct tempo.
successIndicators: Adjust movement and disposal selection collectively.
Maintain active movement during controlled possession.
Accelerate when the defence is displaced.
Match risk to score, time and field position.
matchApplication: Successful teams control when matches speed up and slow down. This simulation develops collective tempo management rather than relying only on the ball carrier’s decision.
relatedDrills: MS-070 – Team Ball Movement Phase Assessment

title: Team Ball Movement Development Stage Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating advanced team ball movement, support and tempo management across continuous match phases.
objective: Assess whether the team can independently apply the advanced team ball-movement behaviours developed in MS-061 to MS-079 during continuous, varied and tactically demanding match simulation.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with interchange players.
Prepare scenario cards covering defensive overload, boundary possession, midfield connection, forward-half retention and defensive line protection.
Prepare tempo instructions for selected phases.
Assign coaches specific team ball-movement behaviours to assess.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Play three blocks of ten to twelve minutes.
Use minimal coach intervention during play.
Require player leaders to conduct short tactical reviews between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the first starting scenario.
Teams organise and begin live play.
Once the initial phase ends, play continues normally.
Coaches assess spacing, support, possession purpose, line connection, tempo and turnover protection.
The coach may introduce a new scenario or tempo instruction during play.
Teams must adapt without a full reset.
At the end of each block, players identify one successful behaviour and one priority correction.
Award points for normal scoring and nominated team ball-movement behaviours.
The final block is played without advance notice of the tactical challenge.
Conclude with individual, line and team ratings against the success indicators.
coachingPoints: Defensive possession should create a launch rather than remain static.
Numerical advantages must create space rather than congestion.
Midfield possession should move the defence and create forward advantage.
Boundary congestion should connect to open-side release.
Overlap running must remain staggered and supported.
Forward-half possession should improve the point of attack.
Defensive lines must remain connected against line-breaking threats.
Centre-square possession should connect with outside runners.
Inside-50 possession should create higher-quality shots.
Tempo must match pressure, space, score and time.
Communication must support every phase change.
Coaches should assess repeated team behaviours rather than isolated successful plays.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Midfield movement used to isolate forwards.

commonErrors.error: Possession creates congestion rather than space.
commonErrors.correction: Improve spacing and involve only the numbers required.

commonErrors.error: The team attacks before the opposition structure is moved.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession until a clear advantage appears.

commonErrors.error: Forward entries are forced despite poor options.
commonErrors.correction: Recycle, switch or use an outlet.

commonErrors.error: Fast ball movement outruns support.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain runners ahead, lateral and behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Defensive coverage disappears during attacking chains.
commonErrors.correction: Keep connected players behind the football.

progressions: Play a full quarter without coach intervention.
Remove all field markers.
Use hidden tactical objectives for each team.
Reduce interchange availability.
Record the assessment for detailed tactical review.
regressions: Use four starting scenarios rather than five.
Announce tempo changes only at stoppages.
Keep visible lane and zone markers.
Provide player leaders with tactical reminder cards.
successIndicators: Create and use defensive numerical advantages.
Move midfield defences to produce forward advantage.
Transfer from boundary congestion to open space.
Release outside runners from centre-square possession.
Create high-quality shots through inside-50 possession.
Maintain width, depth and line connection.
Protect against turnover during attacking ball movement.
Perform advanced team ball movement without continuous coach direction.
matchApplication: This assessment completes the team-ball-movement development stage of the Match Simulation chapter. It determines whether players can integrate overloads, switches, line connections, forward isolation, overlap running, possession retention and tempo management within continuous Australian football.
relatedDrills: MS-075 – Forward-Half Possession Lock and Switch Simulation

title: Scoreboard-Led Possession Strategy Simulation
primarySkill: Adjusting team possession strategy according to score, time and field position.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to select and execute an appropriate possession strategy according to the scoreboard, remaining time, field position and opposition pressure.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Establish a visible scoreboard and countdown clock.
Prepare scenarios including leading by eight points, trailing by four points, scores level and protecting percentage.
Start each scenario from a different field position.
Give teams 20 seconds to confirm their strategy.
Allow normal match rules and live transition.
Rotate player leadership responsibilities.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score, remaining time and starting possession.
Teams communicate their intended possession strategy.
Play begins from the nominated restart or mark.
The team in possession decides whether to retain, gain territory, switch, attack centrally or accelerate.
The opposition attempts to force a turnover and achieve its own scoreboard objective.
Play continues until the scenario time expires, a decisive score occurs or possession becomes dead.
Award three points for achieving the scoreboard objective.
Award one behaviour point for each correct tactical possession decision.
Change the score, time and field position after each repetition.
Complete four to six scenarios.
coachingPoints: Players must know the score and time before possession begins.
Risk should increase or decrease according to the scenario.
Retaining possession must still move the opposition or improve field position.
Boundary use may reduce risk when protecting a lead.
Corridor use may be required when time and score demand rapid attack.
Players behind the football must adjust according to the selected risk level.
Leaders should communicate strategy clearly without controlling every disposal.
Players must recognise when the scenario changes after a score or turnover.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: The relationship between possession strategy and scoreboard need.
Use of boundary, corridor and switch options.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same ball movement in every scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust tempo, width and risk to score and time.

commonErrors.error: The leading team retains possession without improving safety.
commonErrors.correction: Move the opposition and gain useful field position.

commonErrors.error: The trailing team attacks recklessly too early.
commonErrors.correction: Increase risk progressively according to remaining time.

commonErrors.error: Players forget the scoreboard after a turnover.
commonErrors.correction: Reconfirm the required result immediately.

commonErrors.error: All support moves forward during aggressive play.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough defensive coverage to survive a counter-turnover.

progressions: Conceal the exact time and provide verbal time calls.
Change the scoreboard during live play.
Remove coach input and require player leaders to set strategy.
Add interchange or fatigue constraints.
Play a continuous ten-minute block with changing scenarios.
regressions: Use only one lead-protection and one score-chasing scenario.
Pause after marks to discuss options.
Reduce player numbers and ground size.
Provide teams with a preferred tactical plan before play.
successIndicators: Identify score, time and required result.
Adjust risk according to field position.
matchApplication: Possession decisions should change according to the scoreboard rather than remain fixed throughout a match. This simulation develops the tactical judgement required to manage different match states.
relatedDrills: MS-080 – Team Ball Movement Development Stage Assessment

title: Consecutive-Goal Momentum Reset Simulation
primarySkill: Resetting team structure and behaviour after conceding consecutive goals.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to respond calmly and structurally after conceding consecutive goals, stabilise possession and prevent an opposition scoring run from continuing.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Begin with one team recorded as having conceded two consecutive goals.
Restart from the centre square.
Give the recovering team 15 seconds to communicate its reset plan.
The opposition attempts to maintain momentum and score again.
Use a five-minute scenario clock.
Rotate which team manages the momentum reset.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces that one team has conceded two consecutive goals.
Player leaders call the immediate centre-restart and possession plan.
Play restarts from the centre.
The recovering team attempts to win or neutralise the clearance and establish controlled possession.
The opposition applies aggressive pressure to continue its scoring run.
Play continues for five minutes or until one team achieves a nominated outcome.
Award the recovering team three points for preventing another goal and establishing possession.
Award two points for forcing a neutral stoppage or territory gain after the restart.
Award the momentum team three points for scoring another goal.
Review the emotional and tactical response before repeating.
coachingPoints: Players must move immediately from frustration to the next responsibility.
The reset plan should be simple and clearly communicated.
Winning the next possession may be more important than forcing an immediate score.
Centre-square roles must remain disciplined despite emotional pressure.
Players should avoid overcommitting numbers forward.
The team may use possession and territory to reduce opposition momentum.
Leaders must reinforce composure through actions and communication.
One successful defensive or possession phase should become the foundation for normal play.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Emotional response after the scenario announcement.
Decision quality during the first possession.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt to recover the score immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Stabilise possession and field position first.

commonErrors.error: Emotional frustration creates undisciplined centre-square movement.
commonErrors.correction: Return to clear ruck, inside and outside roles.

commonErrors.error: Too many players move ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain balance and protection behind possession.

commonErrors.error: Players stop communicating after another error.
commonErrors.correction: Leaders must reinforce the next action immediately.

commonErrors.error: Possession is rushed because the team feels under pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use simple, high-percentage options to regain control.

progressions: Begin after conceding three consecutive goals.
Start with the opposition already holding midfield possession.
Add a narrow scoreboard margin and limited time.
Remove coach communication completely.
Require the recovering team to stabilise before attacking for a score.
regressions: Begin with the recovering team in controlled possession.
Pause after the centre clearance to discuss the reset.
Provide the team with a pre-planned momentum response.
successIndicators: Win, neutralise or pressure the next possession.
matchApplication: Consecutive opposition goals can create emotional and tactical instability. This simulation teaches teams to interrupt momentum through composure, structure and purposeful possession.

title: Spare Defender Manipulation Simulation
primarySkill: Manipulating and attacking against an opposition spare defender.
objective: Develop the attacking team’s ability to identify an opposition spare defender, move that player away from dangerous space and create a favourable forward entry.
groundSize: From the centre square to the attacking goal.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position the attacking team through midfield and forward 50.
Give the defending team one spare player behind or across the forward contest.
Mark central, deep and opposite-side attacking lanes.
Begin with midfield possession.
The attacking team attempts to identify and move the spare defender before entering.
The defending team attempts to use the spare to intercept and rebound.
Rotate the spare defender and forward match-ups.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team begins with possession near the centre.
Players identify the position and responsibility of the spare defender.
The football is moved laterally, backward or through a high-forward outlet.
Forwards adjust their positions to draw the spare away from the intended entry.
The ball carrier selects the best available entry once a favourable match-up appears.
Play continues until a score, defensive rebound or stoppage.
Award three points for a mark created after moving the spare.
Award four points for a goal from the resulting entry.
Award the defending team three points for an intercept by the spare and controlled rebound.
Reset with the spare in a different starting position.
coachingPoints: Players must identify where the spare defender is positioned.
Possession should move the spare rather than simply move the football.
High forwards may be used to draw or engage the spare.
Deep forwards must maintain separation and avoid leading underneath the spare.
The opposite side should remain available when the spare overcommits.
Entries should target genuine advantage rather than a predetermined player.
Ground-level support remains essential beneath isolated contests.
Midfielders must protect against rebound after the entry.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether possession changes the spare’s position.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier ignores the spare defender.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the defensive structure before entering forward 50.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead into the spare’s area.
commonErrors.correction: Create separation and attack away from the spare.

commonErrors.error: Possession moves without changing the defender’s position.
commonErrors.correction: Use angles and outlets that force the spare to commit.

commonErrors.error: The team targets a predetermined forward regardless of coverage.
commonErrors.correction: Attack the best available match-up.

commonErrors.error: All midfielders move ahead of the entry.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain protection against an intercept rebound.

progressions: Allow the defending team two rotating spare defenders.
Change the spare’s role during the possession chain.
Increase midfield pressure.
Require the attack to produce a shot within 25 seconds.
Continue full-ground play after an intercept.
regressions: Mark the spare defender with a different bib.
Restrict the spare to one zone.
Pause before the entry to identify available space.
successIndicators: Move the spare through purposeful possession.
Create a favourable contest or free receiver.
Support the contest at ground level.
matchApplication: Opposition teams often use a spare defender to intercept forward entries. This simulation develops the patience, movement and tactical awareness required to manipulate that defender.
relatedDrills: MS-075 – Forward-Half Possession Lock and Switch Simulation
MS-078 – Inside-50 Possession Retention and Shot Creation Simulation

title: Tagged Midfielder Release Simulation
primarySkill: Creating possession and influence for a closely tagged midfielder.
