objective: Develop the team’s ability to support a tagged midfielder through legal movement, role rotation and alternative possession methods without damaging overall team structure.
groundSize: Centre square to both 50-metre arcs.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Nominate one midfielder to be closely tagged.
Assign an opposition player to maintain legal close checking.
Position rucks, inside midfielders, wings and half-forwards.
Prepare centre, boundary and around-the-ground stoppages.
Allow teammates to use legal screens, rotations and alternative receiving patterns.
The tagged player must remain defensively accountable.
Rotate tagged and tagging roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins from a nominated stoppage or midfield possession.
The tagger applies close legal attention to the nominated midfielder.
Teammates create movement, screens or role rotations to free the tagged player.
The tagged player may move outside, forward, behind the football or exchange roles.
The team must continue using other midfield options when the tagged player remains covered.
Play continues through a clearance or midfield possession chain.
Award two points when the tagged midfielder receives in usable space.
Award three points when the release contributes to a forward entry.
Award the defending team two points when the tag limits influence without losing team structure.
Reset from a different restart and tactical approach.
coachingPoints: Support must remain legal and avoid holding or blocking off the ball.
The tagged player should vary starting positions and movement patterns.
Teammates must not become obsessed with forcing possession to one player.
Positional rotations can create difficult decisions for the tagger.
The tagged player should continue defending and supporting teammates.
Other midfielders should exploit any space created by the tagging role.
Communication should identify rotations and screening opportunities.
Coaches must monitor off-ball contact closely.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Legality of screens and off-ball contact.
Variety of movement by the tagged player.
Team use of alternative midfield options.
Defensive work by the tagged player.
Whether the tagger maintains team responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Teammates hold or illegally block the tagger.
commonErrors.correction: Use legal body positioning and timed movement only.

commonErrors.error: The tagged player repeats the same lead.
commonErrors.correction: Change depth, side, speed and positional role.

commonErrors.error: The team forces every possession toward the tagged player.
commonErrors.correction: Use the space and alternative options created by the tag.

commonErrors.error: The tagged player stops defending.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain normal defensive and transition responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Rotations occur without communication.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the role exchange before the restart.

progressions: Allow the opposition to change taggers.
Use a full-ground match simulation.
Remove coach direction and require midfield leaders to solve the tag.
Add scoreboard scenarios.
Introduce a second monitored player.
regressions: Restrict the tagger to a smaller area.
Pause before stoppages to plan movement.
matchApplication: Important midfielders are often closely checked. This simulation develops team-based responses that preserve structure and create opportunities without relying on illegal blocking.
relatedDrills: MS-039 – Interchange and Positional Rotation Simulation

title: Temporary Numerical Disadvantage Structure Simulation
primarySkill: Maintaining team structure while temporarily playing with fewer available players.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to protect dangerous space, manage possession and prioritise essential roles during a temporary numerical disadvantage caused by injury, interchange delay or player absence.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Remove one or two players temporarily from one team.
Establish a three- to five-minute disadvantage period.
Begin from defensive, midfield and attacking positions.
The reduced team must adjust roles and protect dangerous space.
The full-number team attempts to identify and exploit the spare.
Rotate which team manages the disadvantage.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the temporary player shortage and its duration.
The reduced team has 20 seconds to reorganise.
Play begins from a nominated restart.
The reduced team manages possession, field position and defensive structure.
The opposition attempts to create and use its numerical advantage.
The missing player returns when the countdown expires.
Award the reduced team three points for preventing a goal during the disadvantage.
Award two points for retaining possession for a nominated period.
Award the full-number team three points for creating a score through the spare player.
Repeat from different field positions and role shortages.
coachingPoints: The reduced team must protect dangerous space before low-threat opponents.
Players should avoid chasing individual opponents across the entire ground.
Possession can reduce the time spent defending.
Tempo and risk should reflect the disadvantage.
The nearest player pressures while others maintain coverage.
Communication must identify the opposition spare.
Players should avoid working beyond safe physical capacity.
Structure must return immediately when equal numbers are restored.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Protection of corridor and goal-side space.
Return to normal structure when numbers equalise.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt to match every opponent directly.
commonErrors.correction: Protect dangerous space and pass low-threat players between roles.

commonErrors.error: The reduced team attacks recklessly.
commonErrors.correction: Manage possession and risk until numbers return.

commonErrors.error: Everyone pressures the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: One pressures while others cover space and receivers.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to identify the opposition spare.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the spare’s location continuously.

commonErrors.error: Structure remains altered after the player returns.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish normal roles immediately.

progressions: Remove two players from one line.
Begin the disadvantage close to defensive goal.
Conceal the exact return time.
Add a narrow scoreboard margin.
Allow the full-number team to change its spare player dynamically.
regressions: Pause after possession changes to reorganise roles.
successIndicators: Restore normal structure when numbers return.
matchApplication: Teams may temporarily play short because of an injury, delayed interchange or player leaving the ground. This simulation prepares players to manage those periods without structural panic.
relatedDrills: MS-076 – Defensive Line-Break Prevention and Rebound Simulation

title: Wind-Affected Quarter Strategy Simulation
primarySkill: Adjusting team strategy and skill execution to strong wind conditions.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to modify possession, kicking, field position and scoring strategy when playing with or against a strong wind.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Identify the actual wind direction or nominate a simulated wind direction.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
One team plays with the wind and the other against it.
Establish a scoreboard and quarter clock.
Mark safe boundary territory zones and central risk zones.
Play two blocks, changing ends between blocks.
Adjust kicking expectations to actual conditions and player safety.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach explains the wind direction and scoreboard scenario.
Play begins from a centre restart.
The team with the wind attempts to maximise territory and scoring opportunities.
The team against the wind attempts to retain possession, use safer angles and limit damage.
Kicking, leading and defensive positioning must adjust to the wind.
Play continues for six to eight minutes.
Teams change ends and roles.
Award normal match points plus behaviour points for correct wind-related decisions.
Review field position, shot selection and turnover locations.
Repeat with a different score or time scenario.
coachingPoints: Players must understand the wind direction before play begins.
With the wind, teams should gain territory without wasting possession.
Against the wind, possession and boundary use may become more valuable.
Kicks should account for drift, carry and reduced accuracy.
Forwards and defenders must position according to likely ball movement.
Long kicks against the wind require organised ground-level support.
Shots should be selected according to range and wind assistance.
Stoppage and kick-in strategy should change with field direction.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scoreboard strategy with and against the wind.

commonErrors.error: Players use normal kicking targets despite strong drift.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust starting line, trajectory and target location.

commonErrors.error: The team with the wind kicks long without purpose.
commonErrors.correction: Use the wind to gain controlled territory and scoring position.

commonErrors.error: The team against the wind forces low-percentage central kicks.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or use safer boundary territory.

commonErrors.error: Forwards stand where the football would travel in calm conditions.
commonErrors.correction: Position according to expected wind movement.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt shots beyond realistic range.
commonErrors.correction: Use a closer option or improve the angle.

progressions: Conceal the scoreboard requirement until play begins.
Add changing or cross-wind conditions.
Use specific kick-in and stoppage scenarios.
Reduce coach communication.
Play a full quarter with ends changed afterward.
regressions: Use a clearly marked simulated wind direction.
Restrict play to half a ground.
Pause after marks to discuss wind options.
Use only one with-wind and one against-wind objective.
successIndicators: Use possession effectively against the wind.
Create scoring pressure with the wind.
matchApplication: Wind can significantly alter the value of possession, territory and scoring opportunities. This simulation develops the tactical flexibility required to manage different ends of the ground.

title: Forward-Half Stoppage Set-Play Simulation
primarySkill: Executing planned attacking methods from forward-half stoppages.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to organise and execute multiple forward-half stoppage methods while maintaining protection against an opposition clearance.
groundSize: Inside attacking 50 and approximately 20 metres outside the arc.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Position rucks, midfielders, forwards and defenders around forward-half stoppages.
Prepare three to five attacking set plays.
Include boundary throw-ins, ball-ups and stoppages near the forward arc.
Assign defensive players realistic match-up and space responsibilities.
Position one or two attacking players outside the immediate stoppage for rebound prevention.
Rotate ruck and midfield combinations.
Allow the defending team to counterattack after winning possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces or signals the attacking stoppage method.
Players organise roles before the restart.
The ruck and midfielders execute the intended hit, movement or release.
Forwards create space for the nominated scoring option.
If the initial method fails, play continues live.
The defending team attempts to win possession and exit defensive 50.
Award three points for a shot created directly from the set play.
Award four points for a goal from the method.
Award the defending team three points for winning the stoppage and exiting.
Reset from a different stoppage position and method.
coachingPoints: Players must understand the purpose of the set play, not only their movement.
Ruck and midfield timing must be precise.
Forwards should create space rather than crowd the intended exit.
Ground-level coverage must account for an imperfect hit.
Players outside the stoppage should protect against defensive release.
The team must transition to normal play if the set method fails.
Different methods should be available for different field positions.
Communication should disguise intent where possible.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing between ruck and midfield movement.
Ability to continue after the set play breaks down.

commonErrors.error: Players memorise movement without understanding the objective.
commonErrors.correction: Explain the scoring space or receiver the method is designed to create.

commonErrors.error: Forwards crowd the planned exit.
commonErrors.correction: Clear the target area before the restart.

commonErrors.error: The ruck hit is treated as guaranteed.
commonErrors.correction: Position for neutral and opposition outcomes.

commonErrors.error: Players stop when the set play fails.
commonErrors.correction: Transition immediately into normal pressure and structure.

commonErrors.error: No one protects against a defensive clearance.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain players outside and behind the stoppage.

progressions: Allow the defence to scout and adjust to the set play.
Use disguised calls and late changes.
Add scoreboard and time scenarios.
Require players to select the method without coach input.
Continue full-ground play after defensive exits.
regressions: Walk through the movement before live execution.
Practise one method from one position.
Pause after the hit to coach forward movement.
successIndicators: Continue playing when the method fails.
matchApplication: Forward-half stoppages offer opportunities to create planned scoring methods. Their value depends on role clarity, timing and the ability to transition when the planned outcome does not occur.

title: Narrow-Lead Protection Simulation
primarySkill: Protecting a narrow lead during the final minutes of a match.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to protect a lead of one to six points through intelligent possession, field position, defensive structure and time management.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Set the protecting team ahead by one to six points.
Set two to four minutes on the countdown clock.
Start from defensive possession, a centre restart, boundary stoppage or opposition forward entry.
The trailing team attempts to create the winning score.
The leading team attempts to protect the margin.
Rotate starting situations and lead sizes.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score, time and starting position.
Teams communicate their tactical approach.
Play begins live.
The leading team manages possession, territory and defensive structure.
The trailing team increases pressure and attacking risk.
Play continues until time expires or the lead changes.
Award the leading team three points for protecting the result.
Award one behaviour point for correct possession, territory or stoppage decisions.
Award the trailing team three points for taking the lead.
Reset with a different margin and starting position.
coachingPoints: Players must know whether conceding a behind changes the result.
Possession should be retained in safe areas.
Boundary use can reduce central turnover risk.
Players should avoid retreating so deeply that the opposition gains repeated entries.
Defenders must protect the most dangerous scoring space.
The team should recognise when territory is more valuable than possession.
Stoppages may help consume time when managed safely.
Leaders must communicate time and score at every pause.

commonErrors.error: Players defend too deeply and invite repeated entries.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough field position and pressure outside defensive 50.

commonErrors.error: The leading team takes unnecessary corridor risk.
commonErrors.correction: Use safer possession unless central play clearly improves the situation.

commonErrors.error: Players kick long to an opposition outnumber.
commonErrors.correction: Identify support or use the boundary for territory.

commonErrors.error: Defenders lose track of the score required.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate whether a goal or any score changes the result.

commonErrors.error: Players rush when the opposition applies pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Stay composed and use the safest effective option.

progressions: Reduce the lead to one point.
Start with the opposition in attacking possession.
Conceal the exact time remaining.
Remove coach communication.
Include repeated centre restarts after scores.
regressions: Increase the lead and remaining time.
Begin with the leading team in uncontested possession.
Pause after marks to discuss risk.
successIndicators: Understand the score and required opposition result.
matchApplication: Protecting a narrow lead requires more than placing numbers behind the football. Teams must balance possession, territory, pressure and defensive structure until the final siren.
relatedDrills: MS-085 – Temporary Numerical Disadvantage Structure Simulation

title: Late Winning-Score Chase Simulation
primarySkill: Creating the required winning score during the final minutes of a match.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to increase attacking urgency and risk intelligently when chasing a winning score without losing all defensive structure.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Set one team behind by one to eleven points.
Set one to four minutes on the countdown clock.
Begin from centre restart, defensive possession, boundary stoppage or opposition possession.
The trailing team attempts to create the required score.
The leading team protects the result.
Rotate the deficit and starting field position.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the score, time and score required.
Teams communicate their tactical plans.
Play begins live.
The trailing team adjusts risk, positioning and tempo.
The leading team attempts to retain possession, gain territory and deny central access.
Play continues until time expires or the result changes.
Award the trailing team three points for achieving the winning score.
Award one behaviour point for creating a high-quality scoring chance.
Award the leading team three points for protecting the result.
Reset with a different deficit and restart type.
coachingPoints: Players must know whether a behind, goal or multiple scores are required.
Risk should rise according to time remaining and field position.
Urgency must not become blind forward kicking.
Players should identify the fastest realistic route to scoring range.
Forwards must preserve width and central scoring space.
Stoppages may need to be won cleanly rather than neutralised.
Players behind the football should still protect against a decisive counter-score.
Leaders must communicate time and score continuously.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Selection of corridor, boundary or long options.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt low-percentage forward kicks immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Create the fastest realistic controlled route to scoring range.

commonErrors.error: The team does not know whether a behind is sufficient.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm the exact score required before the restart.

commonErrors.error: All players move ahead of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain enough coverage to prevent a decisive counter-score.

commonErrors.error: Forwards crowd central scoring space.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve separate leading lanes and goal-square access.

commonErrors.error: The team uses slow possession despite limited time.
commonErrors.correction: Increase tempo and risk according to the clock.

progressions: Reduce the time available.
Begin with the opposition in possession.
Require two scoring events.
Conceal the exact time and provide verbal calls.
Remove coach communication completely.
matchApplication: Late-game attacking football requires controlled urgency. This simulation develops the ability to chase a result without allowing desperation to destroy decision quality.

title: Advanced Tactical Application Assessment
primarySkill: Applying advanced tactical solutions across changing match scenarios.
objective: Assess whether the team can independently identify and execute appropriate tactical solutions across the advanced match situations developed in MS-081 to MS-089.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with interchange players.
Prepare six tactical scenarios selected from MS-081 to MS-089.
Include at least one scoreboard scenario, one structural problem and one opposition tactic.
Assign coaches specific tactical behaviours to assess.
Establish a scoreboard and countdown clock.
Play three blocks of ten to twelve minutes.
Use minimal coach intervention.
Require player leaders to conduct short tactical reviews between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the first tactical scenario.
Teams receive 20 seconds to organise.
Play begins live.
Once the initial scenario is resolved, normal play continues.
Coaches may introduce a second tactical problem during the block.
Teams must identify the change and adjust without a full stoppage.
At the end of each block, players identify the problem, chosen solution and effectiveness.
Award normal match points plus behaviour points for correct tactical responses.
The final block begins with limited information and requires players to diagnose the scenario.
Conclude with individual, line and team ratings against the success indicators.
coachingPoints: Players must diagnose the tactical problem before selecting a solution.
Score, time and field position must influence every plan.
Possession should manage momentum as well as move the football.
Opposition spares and tags should be manipulated rather than ignored.
Numerical disadvantages require role prioritisation and space protection.
Weather and ground conditions should alter execution and risk.
Set plays must transition into normal football when they break down.
Late-game strategy requires clear player leadership.
Coaches should assess decision quality, not only the final outcome.
Tactical responses must remain adaptable when the opposition changes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Manipulation of an opposition spare defender.
Adaptation to wind or altered conditions.

commonErrors.error: Players apply a preferred tactic without diagnosing the problem.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the opposition structure, score and field position first.

commonErrors.error: Teams continue with a plan after the opposition adjusts.
commonErrors.correction: Reassess and select a new method.

commonErrors.error: Tactical complexity reduces basic skill execution.
commonErrors.correction: Use the simplest solution capable of solving the problem.

commonErrors.error: Leaders communicate outcomes rather than roles.
commonErrors.correction: Clarify who performs each tactical responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Players focus only on the scoreboard and lose team structure.
commonErrors.correction: Balance tactical urgency with possession and defensive protection.

progressions: Play a full quarter with hidden tactical objectives.
Allow opposition coaches or player leaders to change structures.
Remove coach feedback between blocks.
Add interchange and fatigue restrictions.
Record the assessment for detailed tactical review.
regressions: Use four scenarios rather than six.
Pause after the first phase to discuss adjustments.
Reduce player numbers and ground size.
Provide leaders with tactical response cards.
successIndicators: Adjust possession to score, time and field position.
Adapt to weather or environmental conditions.
Execute and recover from set plays.
matchApplication: This assessment tests whether players can solve advanced match problems rather than simply execute a predetermined drill. It prepares the team for the tactical variability of competitive Australian football.

title: Full-Quarter Coaching-Box Simulation
primarySkill: Executing team systems across a continuous quarter with match-day coaching conditions.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to maintain tactical structure, respond to match situations and apply limited coaching feedback during a continuous quarter played under realistic match-day conditions.
groundSize: Full ground where available, or a proportionally reduced ground maintaining normal positional relationships.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with interchange players.
Allocate coaches to separate coaching-box or boundary positions.
Nominate line leaders for defence, midfield and attack.
Establish normal interchange procedures and positional rotations.
Use a visible scoreboard and quarter clock.
Coaches may communicate only through designated runners, interchange messages or quarter breaks.
Prepare one tactical focus for each team without revealing the opposition’s focus.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin the quarter from a centre restart.
Play continues under normal match rules for 18–25 minutes according to player age and conditioning.
Coaches observe from designated positions and avoid stopping play.
Tactical messages may be delivered only through approved match-day communication methods.
Players organise stoppages, match-ups, transitions and positional rotations independently.
Interchanges occur under normal live-play conditions.
The scoreboard and clock remain active throughout the quarter.
Coaches record tactical, structural and communication observations.
At the end of the quarter, teams complete a three-minute player-led review.
Coaches then provide one confirmed strength and one priority adjustment.
coachingPoints: Players must organise without constant coach intervention.
Line leaders should connect information across the ground.
Team structure must be maintained during long periods of continuous play.
Players should recognise scoreboard, time and momentum changes.
Interchanges must not create vacant roles or unguarded opponents.
Tactical messages should be simple enough to apply immediately.
Players must retain emotional control after scores, free kicks and errors.
Coaches should observe patterns rather than reacting to isolated mistakes.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Team structure across extended live play.
Player organisation at stoppages and restarts.
Response to scores and momentum changes.
Decision quality late in the quarter.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for instructions from the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Require line leaders to organise immediate match responsibilities.

commonErrors.error: Coaching messages contain too many instructions.
commonErrors.correction: Deliver one clear behavioural or structural adjustment.

commonErrors.error: Team shape deteriorates late in the quarter.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce spacing, role discipline and communication under fatigue.

commonErrors.error: Interchanges leave temporary positional gaps.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm replacement and match-up handover before players exit.

commonErrors.error: Players react emotionally to individual decisions or errors.
commonErrors.correction: Refocus communication on the next contest and team role.

progressions: Play two consecutive quarters with a short break.
Restrict coaching communication further.
Use different tactical objectives for each quarter.
Add official or neutral umpires.
Record the quarter for detailed post-session review.
regressions: Allow one coach stoppage midway through the quarter.
Play on a reduced ground with fewer players.
successIndicators: Adjust to score, time and momentum.
Finish the quarter with tactical discipline.
matchApplication: This simulation recreates the communication, continuity and tactical demands of a match quarter. It tests whether team systems remain functional when coaches cannot stop play and correct every error.

title: Opposition Tactical Change Recognition Simulation
primarySkill: Recognising and responding to an opposition tactical change during live play.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to identify changes in opposition structure or behaviour and implement an appropriate response without waiting for a formal coaching stoppage.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Give one team several hidden tactical-change cards.
Possible changes include an extra defender, higher press, loose player behind the football, midfield tag, attacking overload or boundary-side trap.
Begin with normal match simulation.
At nominated times, one team implements a hidden tactical change.
The opposition must recognise, communicate and respond.
Coaches observe without immediately identifying the change.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a normal restart.
After two to three minutes, one team quietly implements its assigned tactical change.
The opposition continues playing while attempting to identify what has changed.
Player leaders communicate the problem and organise an adjustment.
Play continues for a further two to four minutes.
The coach stops play only after the response has been attempted.
Players state the tactical change they observed and the response they selected.
Award two points for correctly identifying the change.
Award three points for implementing an effective response.
Repeat with a different hidden tactical change.
coachingPoints: Players should observe opposition positioning away from the football.
Tactical recognition must occur through communication across all lines.
Teams should confirm the problem before making large structural changes.
The selected response should remain simple and achievable.
One tactical adjustment should not create a more dangerous weakness elsewhere.
Leaders must communicate roles, not only announce the opposition tactic.
Players should continue executing fundamental skills during tactical problem solving.
Teams must reassess if the opposition changes again.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Awareness of opposition players away from the football.
Whether basic team structure remains intact.
Ability to reassess after the response.

commonErrors.error: Players focus only on the football.
commonErrors.correction: Scan opposition positioning across the entire ground.

commonErrors.error: One player recognises the change but does not communicate it.
commonErrors.correction: Use line leaders to confirm and spread the information.

commonErrors.error: The team overreacts before confirming the tactic.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the repeated pattern before making a major adjustment.

commonErrors.error: The response is too complex to apply during play.
commonErrors.correction: Select one simple structural or match-up change.

commonErrors.error: The adjustment creates an unprotected area elsewhere.
commonErrors.correction: Check corridor, defensive coverage and forward connection after changing.

progressions: Introduce two tactical changes during one playing block.
Allow both teams to make hidden changes.
Remove coach assistance between repetitions.
Add scoreboard and time pressure.
Require teams to disguise their own adjustment.
regressions: Announce the type of change but not its timing.
Pause briefly after the change begins.
Reduce player numbers and ground size.
Allow coaches to ask guided recognition questions.
successIndicators: Reassess the effectiveness of the response.
matchApplication: Opposition teams change structures, match-ups and pressure methods throughout matches. Successful teams recognise these changes quickly and respond before significant damage occurs.

title: Injury and Emergency Role Reallocation Simulation
primarySkill: Reallocating roles and maintaining structure after an unexpected player loss.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to respond safely and efficiently when a player leaves the field unexpectedly through injury, blood rule or equipment issue.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground with a clearly marked interchange area.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two match-simulation teams with interchange players.
Establish emergency replacement chains for key positions.
Begin normal live play.
At unpredictable times, the coach removes a player using an injury or blood-rule signal.
The affected team must protect the temporary gap and organise a replacement.
Removed players do not simulate injury physically; they leave safely through the interchange area.
Rotate the lines and roles affected.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a nominated restart.
During live play, the coach signals one player to leave the ground immediately and safely.
The player communicates the role and direct opponent before exiting where possible.
Nearby teammates temporarily cover the vacant role.
The interchange group identifies and sends the correct replacement.
The replacement enters with knowledge of the role, opponent and current ball position.
Play continues throughout the change.
Award two points for covering the temporary gap.
Award three points for completing the replacement without conceding a structural advantage.
Repeat with different positions and match situations.
coachingPoints: Player safety takes priority over tactical organisation.
The nearest suitable teammate should cover the vacant role temporarily.
Match-up handovers must be communicated clearly.
The interchange group should know emergency replacement chains.
Incoming players must scan the ground before entering.
The team should avoid several players changing roles unnecessarily.
Leaders must identify any temporary numerical disadvantage.
Normal structure should return once the replacement is established.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Immediate coverage of the vacant role.
Communication of direct opponents and responsibilities.
Speed and accuracy of replacement selection.

commonErrors.error: Players focus on the tactical issue before player safety.
commonErrors.correction: Ensure the affected player leaves safely before all other concerns.

commonErrors.error: Several teammates abandon roles to cover one vacancy.
commonErrors.correction: Use the nearest suitable player as a temporary replacement.

commonErrors.error: The direct opponent is left unguarded.
commonErrors.correction: Complete a clear match-up handover immediately.

commonErrors.error: The incoming player enters without knowing the role.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm position, opponent and ball location before entry.

commonErrors.error: The team remains in emergency structure after replacement.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish normal positions and responsibilities.

progressions: Remove a player during a defensive-50 phase.
Simulate two linked role changes.
Delay the replacement entry briefly.
Add a narrow scoreboard margin.
Require player leaders to manage the full response.
regressions: Announce the affected position in advance.
Pause play during the first repetitions.
Provide emergency-role cards to player leaders.
matchApplication: Unexpected player exits can create dangerous temporary gaps. Teams require clear emergency replacement processes to preserve structure while the player receives attention.
relatedDrills: MS-039 – Interchange and Positional Rotation Simulation
MS-085 – Temporary Numerical Disadvantage Structure Simulation
MS-092 – Opposition Tactical Change Recognition Simulation

title: Match-Day Interchange Load Management Simulation
primarySkill: Managing interchanges to maintain player work rate and positional structure.
objective: Develop players and coaches’ ability to complete planned and reactive interchanges while maintaining team balance, role coverage and safe physical workloads.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground with a marked interchange area.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two teams with interchange players.
Prepare planned rotation chains for midfield, wing, forward and defensive roles.
Establish maximum playing blocks appropriate to age and conditioning.
Nominate an interchange manager for each team.
Begin a continuous quarter.
Coaches may call planned or reactive rotations.
Player safety and individual restrictions override the drill objectives.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins from a centre restart.
Interchange managers track player time and planned rotations.
Players communicate when approaching their nominated rotation period.
Outgoing players complete role and match-up handovers.
Incoming players enter with immediate awareness of the current phase.
Coaches may create an unplanned rotation due to simulated fatigue, match-up need or tactical change.
Play continues without drill stoppages.
Award two points for completing each clean rotation chain.
Deduct one behaviour point for a vacant role, duplicated change or interchange communication error.
Review workload balance and structural effects after the quarter.
coachingPoints: Rotations should support performance rather than occur blindly according to a clock.
Players must communicate fatigue honestly and early.
Planned rotation chains should preserve positional coverage.
Outgoing players must hand over direct opponents.
Incoming players should understand the match phase before entering.
Multiple connected players should not leave simultaneously unless planned.
Coaches should monitor individual conditioning, age and return-to-play restrictions.
The team must maintain scoreboard and tactical awareness during rotations.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Communication of fatigue and replacement needs.
Impact of rotations on team performance.

commonErrors.error: Players wait until exhausted before requesting rotation.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate early enough to complete an organised change.

commonErrors.error: Several midfielders rotate simultaneously.
commonErrors.correction: Use staggered rotation chains.

commonErrors.error: Outgoing players leave without handing over opponents.
commonErrors.correction: Confirm responsibility before exiting.

commonErrors.error: Incoming players focus on finding a position rather than current play.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the ball, opponent and team structure before entering.

commonErrors.error: Rotation plans ignore the match situation.
commonErrors.correction: Delay or modify changes when a critical phase requires continuity.

progressions: Reduce interchange availability.
Introduce a restricted total interchange count.
Add specific player-minute targets.
Require player leaders to manage rotations.
Play two consecutive quarters and compare workload distribution.
regressions: Pause briefly for early rotation chains.
Reduce the number of positional rotations.
matchApplication: Effective interchange management supports physical performance and tactical stability. Poorly organised rotations can create structural gaps even when player workloads are well intended.
relatedDrills: MS-039 – Interchange and Positional Rotation Simulation
MS-093 – Injury and Emergency Role Reallocation Simulation

title: Umpiring Interpretation Adaptation Simulation
primarySkill: Adapting player technique and decision making to the way a match is being officiated.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to recognise consistent umpiring interpretations and adjust tackling, marking, stoppage and possession behaviours without arguing or losing concentration.
groundSize: Half to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Use one or more coaches or neutral participants as umpires.
Select an interpretation emphasis for each block, such as holding the ball, protected area, marking interference, high contact or insufficient intent.
Do not announce the emphasis before the first block.
Begin normal match simulation.
Players must recognise the pattern and adjust.
Maintain genuine laws and safe officiating throughout.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins under normal match conditions.
Umpires apply the nominated interpretation consistently.
Players observe repeated decisions and communicate the pattern.
Teams adjust tackling technique, disposal urgency, marking position or boundary decisions.
Play continues for five to seven minutes.
At the block break, players identify the interpretation and required adjustment.
A new emphasis is introduced for the next block.
Award behaviour points for correct adaptation.
Deduct behaviour points for repeated preventable free kicks or dissent.
Complete three to four interpretation blocks.
coachingPoints: Players must respond to consistent officiating rather than debate individual decisions.
Legal tackling technique remains non-negotiable.
Ball carriers should adjust disposal urgency when holding-the-ball decisions are strict.
Players must respect protected areas and stand positions.
Marking defenders should adapt body position without illegal holding.
Leaders should communicate the interpretation calmly.
Dissent distracts players from the next match action.
Adaptation must remain within the laws and spirit of the game.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Adjustment of tackling and possession behaviour.
Respect for protected areas and marks.

commonErrors.error: Players argue each decision instead of identifying the pattern.
commonErrors.correction: Focus on the repeated interpretation and adjust the next action.

commonErrors.error: Tacklers continue using unsafe or high technique.
commonErrors.correction: Lower body position and complete legal tackles.

commonErrors.error: Ball carriers hold possession too long under strict interpretation.
commonErrors.correction: Dispose or create a genuine attempt earlier.

commonErrors.error: Players repeatedly enter protected areas.
commonErrors.correction: Identify the mark location and move outside the required space.

commonErrors.error: Frustration affects the next contest.
commonErrors.correction: Use a team reset call and return to role immediately.

progressions: Use two simultaneous interpretation emphases.
Add neutral umpires unfamiliar to the players.
Introduce a narrow scoreboard margin.
Remove coach feedback between blocks.
Play a full quarter under one consistent interpretation.
regressions: Announce the interpretation before the block.
Pause after free kicks to explain the adjustment.
Reduce player numbers and ground size.
matchApplication: Umpiring interpretations can vary in emphasis between matches. Teams must adapt within the laws rather than allowing frustration or repeated infringements to influence performance.

title: Ground-Dimension Tactical Adaptation Simulation
primarySkill: Adapting team structure and ball movement to different ground dimensions.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to adjust spacing, movement and tactical priorities when playing on grounds that are wider, narrower, longer or shorter than its usual venue.
groundSize: Two or more differently proportioned playing areas marked within the available ground.
equipment: Goal posts or portable scoring posts
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Mark one narrow playing area and one wide playing area.
Where space permits, also vary ground length.
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Prepare tactical objectives for each ground shape.
Play one block in each marked area.
Maintain realistic positional spacing within each shape.
Explain all boundaries clearly before beginning.
howTheDrillWorks:
Play begins in the first ground configuration.
Teams adjust their structures to the available width and length.
The coach observes corridor access, boundary use, defensive shifting and forward spacing.
Play continues for six to eight minutes.
Teams move to the second ground configuration.
Players identify the required tactical changes before play resumes.
Award behaviour points for correct use of space.
Award normal match points for scoring.
Compare ball movement and defensive structure between configurations.
Finish with a player-led discussion of the tactical differences.
coachingPoints: Narrow grounds increase congestion and the value of boundary territory.
Wide grounds increase switching opportunities and defensive running demands.
Longer grounds require stronger line connection and repeat running.
Shorter grounds increase the danger of turnovers close to goal.
Forward spacing must reflect available width and depth.
Defensive lines should adjust their lateral and vertical separation.
Players must understand the dimensions before the match begins.
Tactical adaptation should not remove fundamental team principles.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Team width in each ground shape.

commonErrors.error: Players use normal spacing regardless of ground width.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust lateral positions to the available space.

commonErrors.error: Teams force corridor play on a narrow ground.
commonErrors.correction: Use boundary territory and contest support when central space is congested.

commonErrors.error: Far-side options are ignored on a wide ground.
commonErrors.correction: Preserve width and use switches to move the opposition.

commonErrors.error: Positional lines become disconnected on a long ground.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce gaps and increase linking movement.

commonErrors.error: Players are unaware of shortened scoring distance.
commonErrors.correction: Protect turnovers and adjust shot selection.

progressions: Conceal the next ground shape until the teams arrive.
Change dimensions during a playing block.
Add wind-direction considerations.
Remove coach instruction and require player-led adaptation.
Use a full quarter on an unfamiliar venue.
regressions: Use only narrow and wide configurations.
Pause before play to map positional changes.
successIndicators: Recognise the tactical effect of ground dimensions.
Adjust team width and line spacing.
Apply core team principles in different spaces.
matchApplication: Ground dimensions vary significantly across Australian football venues. Teams that adjust their spacing and strategy can use unfamiliar dimensions as an advantage rather than a disruption.

title: Half-Time Tactical Adjustment Simulation
primarySkill: Analysing first-half performance and applying effective half-time tactical adjustments.
objective: Develop a repeatable half-time process in which players and coaches identify the most important match issue, select an achievable adjustment and apply it during the next period of play.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Play a first-half block of ten to twelve minutes.
Assign observers to record selected behaviours such as clearances, defensive exits, forward entries, turnovers and pressure.
Provide each team with a separate half-time area.
Limit half-time to four to six minutes.
Coaches and players must prioritise no more than two adjustments.
Play a second-half block from a centre restart.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams play the first-half block under normal match conditions.
Coaches and observers record specific examples and simple statistics.
At half-time, player leaders first identify what is working and what requires adjustment.
Coaches confirm or refine the priorities.
The team selects one structural and one behavioural adjustment.
Players confirm individual and line responsibilities.
The second-half block begins immediately.
Observers measure whether the selected behaviours change.
Award behaviour points for successful application.
Finish with a comparison of first-half and second-half performance.
coachingPoints: Half-time feedback must focus on the most influential issues.
Evidence should support the selected adjustment.
Players should contribute observations from the ground.
Adjustments must include clear responsibilities.
Coaches should avoid introducing an entirely new system unnecessarily.
Positive behaviours should be reinforced.
The second-half plan should remain adaptable.
Players must return from the break mentally ready to act immediately.

commonErrors.error: Half-time discussion includes too many issues.
commonErrors.correction: Select the one or two changes with the greatest match impact.

commonErrors.error: Feedback relies on vague impressions.
commonErrors.correction: Use specific examples and simple statistics.

commonErrors.error: The adjustment does not assign responsibility.
commonErrors.correction: Clarify which players or lines perform each action.

commonErrors.error: Players leave the break without restating the plan.
commonErrors.correction: Have leaders summarise the adjustment before returning.

commonErrors.error: The team expects immediate perfection.
commonErrors.correction: Measure improvement in repeated behaviours rather than one result.

progressions: Reduce the half-time period.
Remove coach input until players present their solution.
Give each team incomplete statistics.
Allow the opposition to change tactics in the second half.
Record the simulation for post-session review.
regressions: Provide coaches with prepared adjustment options.
Pause briefly after the first second-half phase.
Play shorter first- and second-half blocks.
successIndicators: Apply changes from the first second-half phase.
Maintain a calm and focused half-time process.
matchApplication: Half-time is a limited opportunity to reinforce strengths and correct significant problems. Effective teams use a clear process rather than delivering excessive or emotional information.
relatedDrills: MS-009 – Coach Observation and Feedback Simulation
MS-092 – Opposition Tactical Change Recognition Simulation

title: Final Five-Minute Multi-Scenario Simulation
primarySkill: Managing multiple changing tactical demands during the final five minutes of a close match.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to adapt immediately when score, possession and tactical requirements change repeatedly during the closing stages of a match.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide players into two balanced teams.
Place five minutes on the countdown clock.
Begin with a narrow scoreboard margin.
Prepare scenario changes such as goal scored, behind scored, free kick, centre restart, player temporarily removed or clock update.
The coach introduces changes only at appropriate match moments.
Teams must continuously reassess what result is required.
Complete three to four five-minute repetitions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach announces the initial score, time and starting position.
Play begins live.
When a score or major stoppage occurs, the scoreboard is updated.
The coach may introduce a realistic additional scenario change.
Teams communicate the new score, time and tactical priority.
Play continues without extended coach instruction.
Award three points to the team achieving the required final result.
Award behaviour points for correct tactical adjustments.
Review the decisive decisions after each repetition.
Repeat with a different initial margin and possession state.
coachingPoints: Players must recalculate the required result after every score.
Tactical risk should change as the clock decreases.
The team in front must balance possession and field position.
The trailing team must create urgency without losing all structure.
Centre-restart roles may change according to the score required.
Boundary stoppages and rushed behinds can have different values in each scenario.
Leaders must communicate exact time and score.
Players should remain composed during rapid scenario changes.

commonErrors.error: Players continue using the previous scenario plan.
commonErrors.correction: Recalculate the required result after every score.

commonErrors.error: The trailing team becomes reckless too early.
commonErrors.correction: Increase risk according to time and field position.

commonErrors.error: The leading team retreats completely into defence.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain possession, territory and pressure outside defensive 50.

commonErrors.error: Players are unsure whether a behind changes the result.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the exact required score at every restart.

commonErrors.error: Emotional reaction delays organisation after a score.
commonErrors.correction: Move immediately to the next restart responsibilities.

progressions: Conceal the exact clock and use verbal time calls.
Add a temporary player-number disadvantage.
Remove coach communication entirely.
Use unexpected umpiring or weather conditions.
Play one uninterrupted final-ten-minute scenario.
regressions: Use one score change per repetition.
Display the required result on a board.
successIndicators: Understand the changing score and time.
matchApplication: Late matches rarely remain tactically static. Scores, stoppages and possession changes can alter the required plan within seconds. This simulation prepares players for that complexity.

title: Player-Led Match Simulation Review
primarySkill: Leading the observation, review and adjustment of team performance during match simulation.
objective: Develop players’ ability to identify performance patterns, deliver constructive feedback and implement team adjustments with minimal coach direction.
groundSize: Two-thirds to full ground.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced tactical coaching, live constraints and active correction
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams.
Nominate player leadership groups for each team.
Assign non-playing or rotating players specific observation roles.
Prepare three match-simulation blocks of six to eight minutes.
Coaches remain observers unless safety or major misunderstanding requires intervention.
Player leaders conduct all between-block reviews.
Use a scoreboard and clear tactical objectives.
howTheDrillWorks:
Teams begin the first live match-simulation block.
Player observers record specific examples of team behaviours.
At the end of the block, leadership groups conduct a two-minute review.
Players identify one strength, one problem and one adjustment.
Leaders assign responsibilities for the next block.
Coaches do not add feedback unless invited or required for safety.
The second and third blocks test whether the adjustment is applied.
Observers measure the selected behaviour.
Teams finish with a player-led full-group review.
Coaches provide a final assessment of the review process rather than controlling its content.
coachingPoints: Player feedback must be specific and behaviour based.
Leaders should invite information from different positional lines.
Reviews should remain brief and focused.
The selected adjustment must assign clear responsibilities.
Players should distinguish structural, skill and effort problems.
Positive behaviours should be reinforced.
Feedback must remain respectful and constructive.
The next block should provide evidence of whether the adjustment worked.

commonErrors.error: Reviews become general motivational speeches.
commonErrors.correction: Identify a specific behaviour, example and correction.

commonErrors.error: Only senior leaders contribute.
commonErrors.correction: Invite observations from defence, midfield, attack and interchange players.

commonErrors.error: Players list too many problems.
commonErrors.correction: Select the issue with the greatest match impact.

commonErrors.error: Feedback blames individuals without a solution.
commonErrors.correction: Describe the team behaviour and assign a constructive action.

commonErrors.error: The next block does not measure the adjustment.
commonErrors.correction: Set one observable success indicator before restarting.

progressions: Remove coaches from the review area.
Rotate leadership groups between blocks.
Use video clips during an extended post-session review.
Require written player self-assessments.
Conduct the process during a full match-length simulation.
regressions: Give leaders a structured review template.
Allow coaches to ask guiding questions.
Nominate the adjustment before the first review.
matchApplication: Mature teams solve problems on the ground and contribute meaningfully during breaks. This simulation develops shared tactical ownership rather than total dependence on coaches.
relatedDrills: MS-009 – Coach Observation and Feedback Simulation

title: Match Simulation Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Integrating all technical, tactical, physical, communication and decision-making requirements of match simulation.
objective: Complete a final assessment of the team’s ability to transfer the full Match Simulation chapter into realistic, continuous Australian football with minimal coach intervention.
groundSize: Full ground where available, or a proportionally reduced ground preserving normal positional and tactical relationships.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert scenarios with multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Divide the squad into two balanced teams with interchange players.
Use normal positional structures, interchange procedures and coaching areas.
Establish a scoreboard and match clock.
Play two to four quarters according to player age, conditioning and session objectives.
Prepare scenario cards covering restarts, turnovers, score changes, tactical adjustments, environmental conditions and temporary player shortages.
Assign coaches and observers specific assessment categories.
Nominate player leadership groups.
Limit coach intervention to quarter breaks, safety issues and concise match-day messages.
howTheDrillWorks:
Begin from a centre restart under normal match conditions.
Play continues as uninterrupted match simulation.
Coaches assess technical execution, structure, decision making, pressure, communication and leadership.
At selected natural breaks, the coach may introduce a realistic scenario condition.
Teams must recognise and respond using player-led organisation.
Interchanges and positional rotations occur live.
Quarter breaks follow a realistic review process.
The scoreboard and clock determine tactical requirements.
The final quarter includes a close-match scenario requiring independent player management.
Conclude with player self-assessment, line review and coach evaluation against the chapter success indicators.
coachingPoints: Players must apply previous chapter principles without waiting for drill-specific instructions.
Team structure should remain recognisable through attack, defence, transition and broken play.
Restarts and stoppages require rapid player-led organisation.
Possession, territory and risk must reflect score, time and field position.
Pressure should be connected, legal and purposeful.
Defensive and forward systems must remain balanced around turnovers.
Tactical adjustments should solve observed match problems.
Communication must occur across all positional lines.
Interchanges and emergencies must not create structural panic.
Coaches should assess transfer, consistency and adaptability rather than isolated highlights.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Team ball movement and line connection.

commonErrors.error: Players revert to individual football when pressure increases.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce team spacing, support and role discipline.

commonErrors.error: Structures work only when the starting scenario is announced.
commonErrors.correction: Assess and organise every naturally occurring match phase.

commonErrors.error: Tactical urgency removes turnover protection.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain connected players behind and around possession.

commonErrors.error: Coaches provide too much live direction.
commonErrors.correction: Allow players to identify and solve match problems.

commonErrors.error: Quarter-break feedback becomes excessive.
commonErrors.correction: Select the most important structural and behavioural priorities.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue reduces communication and legal technique.
commonErrors.correction: Simplify decisions, increase role calls and maintain safe execution.

progressions: Use independent or accredited umpires.
Play a full match-length simulation.
Give each team hidden tactical objectives.
Restrict coach communication to formal breaks.
Record the entire simulation for detailed review.
Invite external coaches to assess selected categories.
regressions: Allow one coach stoppage per quarter.
Reduce contact for returning or mixed-ability players.
Provide player leaders with tactical reminder cards.
Use a reduced ground while preserving positional structure.
successIndicators: Maintain effective attacking and defensive structures.
Create purposeful forward entries and scoring opportunities.
Move the football through connected positional lines.
Adjust tempo, possession and risk to the match situation.
Recognise and respond to opposition tactics.
Manage interchanges and unexpected player losses.
Perform chapter principles in continuous match conditions.
matchApplication: This final assessment measures whether the Match Simulation chapter has transferred into complete football performance. It tests the team’s ability to combine structure, skill, pressure, decision making, communication, leadership and tactical adaptability under realistic match conditions.
relatedDrills: MS-050 – Pressure and Contest Phase Assessment
MS-070 – Team Ball Movement Phase Assessment
MS-080 – Team Ball Movement Development Stage Assessment
